at dampe.explanation: "At dampe" means "to steam". It comes from "damp" (steam). When you talk about cooking, it also means to cook in steam: "Jeg damper grøntsager" (I steam vegetables).

sentence.da: Den varme suppe begynder at **dampe**, når låget løftes.
sentence.en: The hot soup starts to steam when the lid is lifted.

at danne.explanation: "At danne" means "to form". To say people start a government, say: "De danner en regering" (They form a government). Do not mix it up with "at forme" (to shape with your hands): "Jeg former dejen" (I shape the dough).

sentence.da: Vand kan **danne** is, når det bliver meget koldt.
sentence.en: Water can form ice when it gets very cold.

at danse.explanation: "At danse" means "to dance". To say who you dance with, use "med" (with): "Jeg danser med Anna" (I dance with Anna).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **danse** til musikken.
sentence.en: I want to dance to the music.

at date.explanation: "At date" means "to date", as in seeing someone romantically. Do not mix it up with "en dato" (a date on the calendar): "Hvad er datoen i dag?" (What is the date today?).

sentence.da: Hun vil gerne **date** en sød fyr.
sentence.en: She would like to date a nice guy.

at debattere.explanation: "At debattere" means "to debate". To say what people debate, say: "Vi debatterer skolereformen" (We are debating the school reform). Do not mix it up with "at diskutere" (to discuss): "Vi diskuterer, hvad vi skal spise" (We are discussing what to eat).

sentence.da: Politikerne skal **debattere** loven i Folketinget i morgen.
sentence.en: The politicians are going to debate the law in Parliament tomorrow.

at definere.explanation: "At definere" means "to define". To say you set a clear goal, use it with "et mål" (a goal): "Vi definerer et mål for året" (We define a goal for the year).

sentence.da: En ordbog hjælper dig med at **definere** ukendte ord.
sentence.en: A dictionary helps you define unknown words.

at dele.explanation: "At dele" means "to share or divide". When you share something with a person, add "med" (with): "Jeg deler min mad med dig" (I share my food with you). When you divide numbers, use "delt med" (divided by): "Ti delt med to er fem" (Ten divided by two is five).

sentence.da: Vi vil **dele** en pizza.
sentence.en: We want to share a pizza.

at dele ud.explanation: "At dele ud" means "to hand out". It is built from "at dele" (to share) and "ud" (out). To say what is handed out, say: "Læreren deler opgaverne ud" (The teacher hands out the assignments). Do not mix it up with "at dele" (to share), where people use the same thing together: "Vi deler en pizza" (We share a pizza).

sentence.da: Han skal **dele ud** til alle børnene.
sentence.en: He is going to hand things out to all the children.

at delegere.explanation: "At delegere" means "to delegate". To name the person you pass the task to, add "til" (to): "Hun delegerer opgaven til Lars" (She delegates the task to Lars).

sentence.da: En god leder tør **delegere** ansvar til andre.
sentence.en: A good leader dares to delegate responsibility to others.

at deltage.explanation: "At deltage" means "to participate". To say what you take part in, add "i" (in): "Jeg deltager i mødet" (I am taking part in the meeting).

sentence.da: Alle kan **deltage** i kurset gratis.
sentence.en: Everyone can take part in the course for free.

at demonstrere.explanation: "At demonstrere" means "to demonstrate". When you show how something works, say: "Læreren demonstrerer forsøget" (The teacher demonstrates the experiment). When you talk about a protest, it also means "to protest": "Folk demonstrerer foran Christiansborg" (People are demonstrating in front of Christiansborg, the parliament building).

sentence.da: Hun vil **demonstrere**, hvordan maskinen virker.
sentence.en: She will demonstrate how the machine works.

at designe.explanation: "At designe" means "to design". The person who designs is "en designer" (a designer).

sentence.da: Arkitekten skal **designe** et nyt hus.
sentence.en: The architect is going to design a new house.

at dirigere.explanation: "At dirigere" means "to conduct or direct". When you lead an orchestra, say: "Han dirigerer orkestret" (He conducts the orchestra). When you point the way for cars, say: "Politiet dirigerer trafikken" (The police are directing traffic). For a film, use "at instruere" (to direct a film) instead: "Hun instruerer en film" (She directs a film).

sentence.da: Han skal **dirigere** koret ved koncerten i aften.
sentence.en: He is going to conduct the choir at the concert tonight.

at diskutere.explanation: "At diskutere" means "to discuss". To say people argue angrily, use "at skændes" (to quarrel): "De skændes hele tiden" (They quarrel all the time).

sentence.da: Vi skal **diskutere** problemet med læreren.
sentence.en: We have to discuss the problem with the teacher.

at distrahere.explanation: "At distrahere" means "to distract". To say someone does it on purpose, say: "Tyven distraherede vagten" (The thief distracted the guard).

sentence.da: Telefonen kan **distrahere** dig, når du laver lektier.
sentence.en: The phone can distract you when you do homework.

at dividere.explanation: "At dividere" means "to divide". To say what you divide by, use "med" (by): "Vi dividerer tallet med to" (We divide the number by two).

sentence.da: Du skal **dividere** tolv med tre.
sentence.en: You have to divide twelve by three.

at dokumentere.explanation: "At dokumentere" means "to document". It comes from the noun "et dokument" (a document). To say what you prove something with, use "med" (with): "Vi dokumenterer resultaterne med billeder" (We document the results with photos).

sentence.da: Du skal **dokumentere** dine udgifter med kvitteringer.
sentence.en: You must document your expenses with receipts.

at dominere.explanation: "At dominere" means "to dominate". To say a person talks the most in a conversation: "Han dominerer samtalen" (He dominates the conversation). To say a color stands out most in a picture: "Blå dominerer billedet" (Blue dominates the picture).

sentence.da: Det bedste hold kan **dominere** kampen fra første minut.
sentence.en: The best team can dominate the match from the first minute.

at donere.explanation: "At donere" means "to donate". To name who receives the gift, add "til" (to): "Jeg donerer penge til Røde Kors" (I donate money to the Red Cross).

sentence.da: Mange vil gerne **donere** blod, fordi det kan redde liv.
sentence.en: Many people want to donate blood because it can save lives.

at downloade.explanation: "At downloade" means "to download". The Danish verb ends in "e", unlike the English "to download". To say you get an app onto your phone: "Jeg downloader en app" (I download an app).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **downloade** en film til min telefon.
sentence.en: I want to download a movie to my phone.

at drage.explanation: "At drage" means "to draw (a conclusion) or go". To say you benefit from something, use "at drage fordel af" (to benefit from): "Vi drager fordel af den nye metro" (We benefit from the new metro). To say people set off for a place, use "at drage til" (to go to): "De drog til Paris" (They went to Paris).

sentence.da: Efter testen kan vi **drage** en klar konklusion.
sentence.en: After the test, we can draw a clear conclusion.

at dreje.explanation: "At dreje" means "to turn". To say what something is about, use "at dreje sig om" (to be about): "Det drejer sig om penge" (It is about money).

sentence.da: Du skal **dreje** til venstre ved banken.
sentence.en: You have to turn left at the bank.

at drikke.explanation: "At drikke" means "to drink". To offer someone a drink, ask: "Vil du have noget at drikke?" (Would you like something to drink?).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **drikke** et glas vand.
sentence.en: I want to drink a glass of water.

at drille.explanation: "At drille" means "to tease". To say someone is teased in a playful way: "Han driller sine venner" (He teases his friends). Teasing that hurts is "at mobbe" (to bully): "Hun bliver mobbet i skolen" (She is bullied at school).

sentence.da: Min bror elsker at **drille** mig.
sentence.en: My brother loves to tease me.

at drive.explanation: "At drive" means "to run (a business) or drift". To say you run a shop: "Hun driver en butik" (She runs a shop). To say something is carried along by wind or water: "Skyerne driver hen over himlen" (The clouds drift across the sky).

sentence.da: Hun vil **drive** sin egen café på havnen.
sentence.en: She wants to run her own cafe at the harbor.

at droppe.explanation: "At droppe" means "to drop or skip". It comes from the English verb "to drop". To say you give up a plan: "Vi dropper planen" (We are dropping the plan).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **droppe** sukker i min kaffe.
sentence.en: I want to skip sugar in my coffee.

at drukne.explanation: "At drukne" means "to drown". In the past, use "er" (am/is), not "har" (have): "Manden er druknet" (The man has drowned).

sentence.da: Man kan **drukne** i dybt vand.
sentence.en: You can drown in deep water.

at dryppe.explanation: "At dryppe" means "to drip". To say water falls from something in drops: "Det drypper fra taget" (It drips from the roof). To say you put drops of something on food: "at dryppe citronsaft på fisken" (to drip lemon juice on the fish).

sentence.da: Hanen i køkkenet kan **dryppe** hele natten.
sentence.en: The tap in the kitchen can drip all night.

at drysse.explanation: "At drysse" means "to sprinkle". To say what you sprinkle something on, use "på" (on): "Jeg drysser sukker på kagen" (I sprinkle sugar on the cake).

sentence.da: Man kan **drysse** kanel over risengrød.
sentence.en: You can sprinkle cinnamon over rice pudding.

at dræbe.explanation: "At dræbe" means "to kill". To say someone was killed, Danish uses "blev" (was) with "dræbt" (killed): "Han blev dræbt" (He was killed).

sentence.da: Ræven kan **dræbe** en høne.
sentence.en: The fox can kill a hen.

at drøfte.explanation: "At drøfte" means "to discuss". To say you discuss a topic, put the topic straight after it: "Vi drøfter budgettet" (We are discussing the budget). The verb "at tale om" (to talk about) needs "om" (about): "Vi taler om budgettet" (We are talking about the budget).

sentence.da: Bestyrelsen skal **drøfte** forslaget på næste møde.
sentence.en: The board must discuss the proposal at the next meeting.

at drømme.explanation: "At drømme" means "to dream". To say what you dream while asleep, use "om" (about): "Jeg drømte om dig" (I dreamed about you). To say what you wish for in life: "Hun drømmer om at rejse" (She dreams of traveling).

sentence.da: Jeg vil sove og **drømme** hele natten.
sentence.en: I want to sleep and dream all night.

at dufte.explanation: "At dufte" means "to smell (nice)". To say what a smell is like, use "af" (of): "Det dufter af kaffe" (It smells of coffee). For a bad smell, use "at lugte" (to smell): "Det lugter af fisk" (It smells of fish).

sentence.da: Det plejer at **dufte** dejligt her.
sentence.en: It usually smells lovely here.

at duge.explanation: "At duge" means "to be any good or work". To say something will not do: "Det duer ikke" (That will not do). To say a tool is no good for a job, use "til" (for): "Den kniv duer ikke til brød" (That knife is no good for bread). A mix-up: "duer" is also the plural of "en due" (a dove): "Duerne sidder på taget" (The doves sit on the roof).

forms.en: I have been any good / worked

sentence.da: Den gamle cykel vil ikke **duge** til så lang en tur.
sentence.en: The old bike will not do for such a long trip.

at dukke op.explanation: "At dukke op" means "to show up". To say someone did not come to an event: "Han dukkede ikke op til mødet" (He did not show up for the meeting). To say something appears on a screen, it means "to pop up": "En besked dukker op" (A message pops up).

sentence.da: Jeg håber, at han vil **dukke op** i aften.
sentence.en: I hope that he will show up tonight.

at dumpe.explanation: "At dumpe" means "to fail (an exam)". To say which exam, use "til" (at): "Han dumpede til eksamen" (He failed the exam). The opposite is "at bestå" (to pass): "Hun bestod eksamen" (She passed the exam).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **dumpe** til eksamen.
sentence.en: I don't want to fail the exam.

at dykke.explanation: "At dykke" means "to dive", as in going under water: "Vi dykker ved koralrevet" (We dive at the coral reef). To dive in headfirst from a board, say "at stupe" (to dive in): "Han stuper fra vippen" (He dives from the board).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **dykke** og se fiskene i havet.
sentence.en: I would like to dive and see the fish in the sea.

at dyppe.explanation: "At dyppe" means "to dip". To leave something in water for a long time, use "at lægge i blød" (to soak): "Jeg lægger bønnerne i blød" (I soak the beans).

sentence.da: Børnene elsker at **dyppe** pommes frites i ketchup.
sentence.en: The children love to dip french fries in ketchup.

at dyrke.explanation: "At dyrke" means "to grow or practice (a sport)". To say you grow plants on purpose: "Vi dyrker tomater" (We grow tomatoes). To say you do a hobby or sport: "Jeg dyrker yoga" (I do yoga).

sentence.da: Min mor vil **dyrke** grøntsager i haven.
sentence.en: My mother wants to grow vegetables in the garden.

at dyrke sport.explanation: "At dyrke sport" means "to do sports". It is built from "at dyrke" (to practice) and "sport" (sports). To say you play one named ball sport, use "at spille" (to play): "Jeg spiller tennis" (I play tennis).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **dyrke sport** mere i år.
sentence.en: I want to do more sports this year.

at dække.explanation: "At dække" means "to cover". To say an insurance company pays for a loss: "Forsikringen dækker skaden" (The insurance covers the damage).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **dække** barnet med et tæppe.
sentence.en: I want to cover the child with a blanket.

at dække bord.explanation: "At dække bord" means "to set the table". It is built from "at dække" (to cover) and "bord" (table). To ask someone to help before dinner: "Kan du dække bord til aftensmad?" (Can you set the table for dinner?)

sentence.da: Jeg skal **dække bord** til fem personer.
sentence.en: I have to set the table for five people.

at dække over.explanation: "At dække over" means "to cover up", as in keeping a mistake hidden. To say you protect someone by staying quiet about what they did: "Hun dækkede over sin bror" (She covered for her brother).

sentence.da: Han ville **dække over** fejlen, men sandheden kom frem.
sentence.en: He wanted to cover up the mistake, but the truth came out.

at dæmpe.explanation: "At dæmpe" means "to dampen or turn down". To say you make a light softer: "Vi dæmper lyset" (We dim the lights). To tell a person to tone it down: "Dæmp dig!" (Tone it down!)

sentence.da: Du må gerne **dæmpe** musikken, når naboerne sover.
sentence.en: You may turn the music down when the neighbors are asleep.

at dø.explanation: "At dø" means "to die". To say someone has died, Danish uses "er" (is) instead of "har" (has): "Han er død" (He has died; literally, "He is dead").

sentence.da: Planter kan **dø** uden vand.
sentence.en: Plants can die without water.

at døbe.explanation: "At døbe" means "to baptize". To say someone was baptized with a name: "Hun blev døbt Maria" (She was baptized Maria). To say you gave a name to an animal: "Vi døbte hunden Bølle" (We named the dog Bølle).

sentence.da: Præsten skal **døbe** barnet på søndag.
sentence.en: The priest will baptize the child on Sunday.

at dømme.explanation: "At dømme" means "to judge or sentence". To say a court found someone guilty, use "for" (for) with the crime: "Han blev dømt for tyveri" (He was convicted of theft). To say you form an opinion of people: "Man skal ikke dømme folk på udseendet" (You should not judge people by their looks).

sentence.da: Retten kan **dømme** ham til to års fængsel.
sentence.en: The court can sentence him to two years in prison.

da.explanation: "Da" means "when", for something that happened once in the past. For something that happens every time or has not happened yet, use "når" (when) instead: "Når jeg kommer hjem, laver jeg mad" (When I get home, I cook).

sentence.da: **Da** jeg kom hjem, sov børnene.
sentence.en: When I came home, the children were asleep.

dagen efter.explanation: "Dagen efter" means "the day after". To say which day it was, name the earlier event after it: "dagen efter eksamen" (the day after the exam). To say the next day without naming an event, use "næste dag" (next day): "Næste dag tog vi hjem" (The next day we went home).

forms.en: The day after, he came home

sentence.da: Jeg var træt **dagen efter** festen.
sentence.en: I was tired the day after the party.

dagens ret.explanation: "Dagens ret" means "dish of the day". It is built from "dagens" (the day's) and "ret" (dish). To ask a waiter about it: "Hvad er dagens ret?" (What is the dish of the day?)

sentence.da: **Dagens ret** er fisk og kartofler.
sentence.en: The dish of the day is fish and potatoes.

dagevis.explanation: "Dagevis" means "for days". The ending "-vis" works the same in other words, such as "timevis" (for hours) and "ugevis" (for weeks).

sentence.da: Efter stormen var der **dagevis** uden strøm.
sentence.en: After the storm there was no power for days.

daglig.explanation: "Daglig" means "daily" and goes before the thing that happens every day: "en daglig avis" (a daily newspaper). To say how often you do something, use "hver dag" (every day): "Jeg løber hver dag" (I run every day).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **daglig** gåtur.
sentence.en: I take a daily walk.

dagligdags.explanation: "Dagligdags" means "everyday". To talk about the language people use in normal conversation, use it with "sprog" (language): "dagligdags sprog" (everyday language). A mix-up: "daglig" (daily) says something happens each day, as in "en daglig tur" (a daily walk). "Dagligdags" says something is ordinary, as in "en dagligdags hændelse" (an everyday event).

sentence.da: Indkøb og madlavning er **dagligdags** ting.
sentence.en: Shopping and cooking are everyday things.

dagligt.explanation: "Dagligt" means "daily". To say how often someone does something, put it after the verb: "Jeg læser dagligt" (I read every day). In front of a thing, use "daglig" with an en-word and "dagligt" with an et-word: "en daglig tur" (a daily walk), "et dagligt møde" (a daily meeting).

sentence.da: Han træner **dagligt** og spiser sundt.
sentence.en: He trains daily and eats healthily.

dagligvarer.explanation: "Dagligvarer" means "the groceries". It is built from "daglig" (daily) and "varer" (goods).

sentence.da: Jeg køber **dagligvarer** i supermarkedet.
sentence.en: I buy groceries at the supermarket.

dagpenge.explanation: "Dagpenge" means "unemployment benefits". Literally, the word means "day money". In Denmark, you only get them if you are a member of an "a-kasse" (an unemployment insurance fund).

sentence.da: Når man bliver fyret, kan man få **dagpenge** i en periode.
sentence.en: When you get fired, you can get unemployment benefits for a period.

dagslys.explanation: "Dagslys" means "daylight". It is built from "dag" (day) and "lys" (light). To say a room is bright enough without lamps: "Der er rigeligt dagslys i stuen" (There is plenty of daylight in the living room).

sentence.da: Om vinteren er der kun få timer med **dagslys**.
sentence.en: In winter there are only a few hours of daylight.

damp.explanation: "Damp" means "steam". The part "damp" also appears in other words, such as "en dampbåd" (a steamboat) and "en dampmaskine" (a steam engine).

forms.en: There is steam in the bathroom.

sentence.da: Når vand koger, bliver det til **damp**.
sentence.en: When water boils, it turns into steam.

dansk.explanation: "Dansk" means "Danish", the language and also things from Denmark: "dansk ost" (Danish cheese). As a school subject, it is used without an article: "Jeg har dansk" (I have Danish class). Language names start with a lowercase letter: "dansk" (Danish), "engelsk" (English).

sentence.da: Jeg bor i Danmark og taler **dansk**.
sentence.en: I live in Denmark and speak Danish.

data.explanation: "Data" means "data". To say you collect data, use "at indsamle" (to collect): "Vi indsamler data" (We collect data).

sentence.da: Vi bruger **data** fra mange mennesker.
sentence.en: We use data from many people.

datalogi.explanation: "Datalogi" means "computer science". It is built from "data" (data) and the ending "-logi" (study of). The same ending is in "biologi" (biology) and "psykologi" (psychology).

sentence.da: Hun læser **datalogi** og lærer at skrive programmer.
sentence.en: She studies computer science and learns to write programs.

datid.explanation: "Datid" means "a past tense". To tell someone to use it, say "i datid" (in the past tense): "Skriv sætningen i datid" (Write the sentence in the past tense). For the past as a period of history, use "fortid" (the past): "Vikingerne boede her i fortiden" (The Vikings lived here in the past).

forms.da: datiden af at gå er gik
forms.en: the past tense of at gå is gik

sentence.da: Ordet spiste står i **datid**, fordi det allerede er sket.
sentence.en: The word spiste is in the past tense because it has already happened.

davs.explanation: "Davs" means "hi", a short, casual greeting for friends and people you know well. With someone you have just met, say "hej" (hi): "Hej, jeg hedder Anna" (Hi, my name is Anna).

sentence.da: **Davs**, Peter! Hvordan går det?
sentence.en: Hi, Peter! How is it going?

de.explanation: "De" means "they". To say they do something, use "de": "De ser mig" (They see me). To say you do something to them, use "dem" (them): "Jeg ser dem" (I see them). "De" is also "the" before more than one thing when a word like "store" (big) comes first: "de store huse" (the big houses).

sentence.da: Anna og Lars? **De** er hjemme.
sentence.en: Anna and Lars? They are at home.

december.explanation: "December" means "December". Danish writes month names with a lowercase letter, so you write "i december" (in December), not "i December". In Denmark, people celebrate Christmas on the evening of 24 December, called "juleaften" (Christmas Eve).

sentence.da: Vi fejrer jul i **december**.
sentence.en: We celebrate Christmas in December.

dedikeret.explanation: "Dedikeret" means "dedicated". It comes from the verb "at dedikere" (to dedicate). To say a thing is made for one task only: "en dedikeret server" (a dedicated server).

sentence.da: Hun er en **dedikeret** lærer og bruger mange timer på sine elever.
sentence.en: She is a dedicated teacher and spends many hours on her pupils.

defekt.explanation: "Defekt" means "defective". To say you can swap a faulty item in a shop: "Du kan bytte en defekt vare" (You can exchange a defective item). A mix-up: "ødelagt" (broken) says something was damaged: "Min telefon er ødelagt" (My phone is broken).

sentence.da: Vaskemaskinen er **defekt**, og den vil ikke starte.
sentence.en: The washing machine is defective, and it will not start.

dejlig.explanation: "Dejlig" means "lovely". To say you are glad to meet someone: "Dejligt at møde dig" (Nice to meet you). To say the weather is lovely: "Det er dejligt vejr" (It is lovely weather).

sentence.da: Det er en **dejlig** varm sommerdag.
sentence.en: It is a lovely warm summer day.

dels ... dels.explanation: "Dels ... dels" means "partly ... partly", for listing two reasons or sides that each matter. At the start of a sentence, the verb comes right after the first "dels" (partly): "Dels er det dyrt, dels er det svært" (Partly it is expensive, partly it is hard).

forms.da: dels for sjov, dels for pengene
forms.en: partly for fun, partly for the money
partly at home, partly at the office

related.da: på den ene side ... på den anden side
related.en: on the one hand ... on the other

sentence.da: Hvorfor jeg bor her? **Dels ... dels**: jobbet og familien.
sentence.en: Why do I live here? Partly ... partly: the job and the family.

deltagelse.explanation: "Deltagelse" means "participation". It is the noun for the verb "at deltage" (to take part). To thank someone for coming, use "i" (in) before the event: "Tak for din deltagelse i kurset" (Thank you for your participation in the course).

sentence.da: Din **deltagelse** i mødet er vigtig for os.
sentence.en: Your participation in the meeting is important to us.

dem.explanation: "Dem" means "them". To say something is done to them: "Jeg hjælper dem" (I help them). To say they do something, use "de" (they): "De ser mig" (They see me).

sentence.da: Mine naboer er søde. Jeg kender **dem**.
sentence.en: My neighbors are nice. I know them.

demokratisk.explanation: "Demokratisk" means "democratic". It comes from the noun "et demokrati" (a democracy). To say people decide something together: "en demokratisk proces" (a democratic process).

sentence.da: I et **demokratisk** land vælger folket selv sine politikere.
sentence.en: In a democratic country, the people choose their own politicians.

den.explanation: "Den" means "it" for words that take "en": "Jeg har en bil. Den er rød" (I have a car. It is red). For words that take "et", use "det" (it): "Jeg har et hus. Det er rødt" (I have a house. It is red). "Den" also means "the" before a describing word: "den røde bil" (the red car).

sentence.da: Se på bilen! **Den** er meget stor.
sentence.en: Look at the car! It is very big.

den offentlige sektor.explanation: "Den offentlige sektor" means "the public sector". To say someone works somewhere else, use the opposite, "den private sektor" (the private sector): "Min søster arbejder i den private sektor" (My sister works in the private sector).

forms.da: at arbejde i den offentlige sektor
forms.en: to work in the public sector

sentence.da: Lærere og sygeplejersker arbejder i **den offentlige sektor**.
sentence.en: Teachers and nurses work in the public sector.

den tid, den sorg.explanation: "Den tid, den sorg" means "We'll cross that bridge when we come to it". Word for word, it means "that time, that sorrow". To brush off a worry about the future: "Hvad hvis det regner?" "Den tid, den sorg." (What if it rains? We will deal with that if it happens.)

forms.en: We'll cross that bridge when we come to it

forms.da: Det tager vi, når det sker
forms.en: We'll deal with that when it happens

forms.da: Hvad hvis det går galt? Den tid, den sorg
forms.en: What if it goes wrong? We'll cross that bridge when we come to it

sentence.da: Måske bliver det dyrt senere, men **den tid, den sorg**.
sentence.en: Maybe it will get expensive later, but we'll cross that bridge when we come to it.

dengang.explanation: "Dengang" means "back then". It is built from "den" (that) and "gang" (time), so it literally means "that time". To say back when something was true, start a clause with it: "dengang jeg var barn" (back when I was a child).

forms.en: What were you doing back then?
My father lived here back then.

sentence.da: **Dengang** boede vi i Odense og var glade.
sentence.en: Back then we lived in Odense and were happy.

denim.explanation: "Denim" means "denim". Another Danish word for jeans is "cowboybukser" (literally, cowboy trousers). To say what something is made of: "Tasken er lavet af denim" (The bag is made of denim).

sentence.da: Jakken er af **denim**, og den holder i mange år.
sentence.en: The jacket is made of denim, and it lasts for many years.

denne.explanation: "Denne" means "this" with words that take "en": "denne bil" (this car). For words that take "et", use "dette" (this): "dette hus" (this house). Another way to say the same thing with an en-word is "den her bil" (this car).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have **denne** bil.
sentence.en: I want this car.

dens.explanation: "Dens" means "its", for something you say with "en", like "en bil" (a car) or "en stol" (a chair). For something you say with "et", use "dets" (its): "Huset er gammelt, men dets tag er nyt" (The house is old, but its roof is new).

sentence.da: Bilen er gammel, men **dens** motor er stærk.
sentence.en: The car is old, but its engine is strong.

deprimerende.explanation: "Deprimerende" means "depressing". To say what causes the feeling: "en deprimerende film" (a depressing movie). To say how a person feels, use "deprimeret" (depressed): "Jeg er deprimeret" (I am depressed).

sentence.da: Regnen og mørket om vinteren kan være **deprimerende**.
sentence.en: The rain and darkness in winter can be depressing.

deprimeret.explanation: "Deprimeret" means "depressed". To say how long a person has felt this way: "Hun har været deprimeret i flere måneder" (She has been depressed for months). To say what causes the feeling, use "deprimerende" (depressing): "en deprimerende film" (a depressing movie).

sentence.da: Han føler sig **deprimeret** og har ikke lyst til at se nogen.
sentence.en: He feels depressed and does not want to see anyone.

der.explanation: "Der" means "there". To say where someone is: "Han er der" (He is there). For the place where you are, use "her" (here): "Han er her" (He is here). To say something exists, start the sentence with it: "Der er mange børn" (There are many children). In the middle of a sentence it can also mean "who": "manden, der bor her" (the man who lives here).

sentence.da: **Der** er en kat i haven.
sentence.en: There is a cat in the garden.

der er ingen ko på isen.explanation: "Der er ingen ko på isen" means "There is nothing to worry about". Word for word, it says there is no cow on the ice. To say there is trouble, take away "ingen" (no): "Der er ko på isen" (There is trouble).

forms.da: Der er ingen ko på isen
forms.en: There is nothing to worry about

forms.da: Rolig, der er ingen ko på isen
Der er ingen ko på isen, vi har god tid
forms.en: There's nothing to worry about, we have plenty of time

sentence.da: Alt er klaret, og **der er ingen ko på isen**.
sentence.en: Everything is taken care of, and there is nothing to worry about.

derefter.explanation: "Derefter" means "after that": "Jeg spiste, og derefter gik jeg" (I ate, and after that I left). To name the earlier event, use "efter" (after) in front of it: "efter maden" (after the meal).

sentence.da: Først mad, og **derefter** kaffe.
sentence.en: First food, and after that coffee.

deres.explanation: "Deres" means "their": "Det er deres hus" (It is their house). Write "deres" the same way before one thing or several: "deres hund" (their dog), "deres hunde" (their dogs).

sentence.da: Anna og Bo bor i **deres** hus.
sentence.en: Anna and Bo live in their house.

derfor.explanation: "Derfor" means "that is why". To give the reason first and the result second: "Jeg er syg, derfor bliver jeg hjemme" (I am sick, that is why I am staying home). To give the result first, use "fordi" (because): "Jeg bliver hjemme, fordi jeg er syg" (I am staying home because I am sick).

forms.en: that is why I am here

sentence.da: Det regner. **Derfor** er jeg hjemme.
sentence.en: It is raining. That is why I am home.

derfra.explanation: "Derfra" means "from there". It is built from "der" (there) and "fra" (from). To say you are a stranger to a place, use "herfra" (from here): "Jeg er ikke herfra" (I am not from here). To say where your family comes from: "Min familie kommer derfra" (My family comes from there).

forms.en: What can you see from there?

sentence.da: Aarhus er flot. Min mor kommer **derfra**.
sentence.en: Aarhus is beautiful. My mother comes from there.

derhen.explanation: "Derhen" means "there". To say you go toward a place, use it after the verb: "Vi cykler derhen" (We cycle there). To name the place where a person stays, use "der" (there): "Han er der" (He is there).

sentence.da: Skal vi gå **derhen** sammen?
sentence.en: Shall we walk there together?

derhjemme.explanation: "Derhjemme" means "at home". To talk about home when you are somewhere else: "Hvad spiser I derhjemme?" (What do you eat at home?). To say you are in your house right now, use "hjemme" (at home): "Jeg er hjemme" (I am at home).

forms.en: what do you do at home?

sentence.da: **Derhjemme** spiser vi sent.
sentence.en: At home we eat late.

derimod.explanation: "Derimod" means "on the other hand". It shows a contrast with what was just said. To put the contrast after the verb: "Min bror er høj. Jeg er derimod lav." (My brother is tall. I, on the other hand, am short.) To put it right after the person: "Min søster derimod er lav" (My sister, on the other hand, is short).

forms.da: Prisen er høj. Kvaliteten derimod er god.
forms.en: The price is high. The quality, on the other hand, is good.
You, on the other hand, are right

sentence.da: Byen er larmende. Landet er **derimod** stille.
sentence.en: The city is noisy. The countryside, on the other hand, is quiet.

derinde.explanation: "Derinde" means "in there". It is built from "der" (there) and "inde" (inside). To say where someone is in another room: "Katten er derinde" (The cat is in there). For the room you are in, use "herinde" (in here): "Jeg er herinde" (I am in here).

forms.en: in there in the living room

sentence.da: Min mor er **derinde** i stuen.
sentence.en: My mother is in there in the living room.

dermed.explanation: "Dermed" means "with that". It is built from "der" (there) and "med" (with). To say what follows from something you just did: "Han skrev under, og dermed er aftalen indgået" (He signed, and with that the deal is made).

sentence.da: Vi har betalt, og **dermed** er sagen afgjort.
sentence.en: We have paid, and with that the matter is settled.

dernede.explanation: "Dernede" means "down there". To say where something is in a lower place: "Katten er dernede" (The cat is down there). For a higher place, use "deroppe" (up there): "Katten er deroppe" (The cat is up there).

sentence.da: Bilen står **dernede** i kælderen.
sentence.en: The car is down there in the basement.

dernæst.explanation: "Dernæst" means "next". To list steps in order, say it after "først" (first): "Først kommer maden, dernæst kommer kaffen" (First comes the food, next comes the coffee).

sentence.da: Først skærer du løget, og **dernæst** steger du det i smør.
sentence.en: First you cut the onion, and then you fry it in butter.

deroppe.explanation: "Deroppe" means "up there". To say where something is in a higher place: "Vores lejlighed ligger deroppe" (Our apartment is up there). For the place where you are, use "heroppe" (up here): "Heroppe er der koldt" (It is cold up here).

forms.en: The cat is sitting up there

sentence.da: Kan du se fuglen **deroppe** i træet?
sentence.en: Can you see the bird up there in the tree?

derovre.explanation: "Derovre" means "over there". To point to a place at a distance: "Bogen ligger derovre" (The book is over there). To say you go there, use "derover" (over there, with movement): "Jeg går derover" (I am going over there).

sentence.da: Min bil står **derovre** ved huset.
sentence.en: My car is parked over there by the house.

derude.explanation: "Derude" means "out there". To say where children are outside: "Børnene er derude" (The children are out there). For inside something, use "derinde" (in there): "Børnene er derinde" (The children are in there).

sentence.da: Se ud af vinduet! Børnene leger **derude**.
sentence.en: Look out of the window! The children are playing out there.

derudover.explanation: "Derudover" means "in addition". At the start of a sentence, the verb follows right after it: "Derudover er prisen lav" (In addition, the price is low).

forms.en: In addition, we have a garden

sentence.da: Han arbejder på kontoret, og **derudover** passer han en lille butik.
sentence.en: He works at an office, and in addition he runs a small shop.

design.explanation: "Design" means "design". It takes "et" in the singular, and with "the" on the end it is "designet" (the design). To say what field someone works in: "Hun arbejder med design" (She works in design). Danish furniture and lamps are known abroad as "dansk design" (Danish design).

sentence.da: Jeg kan lide stolens **design** og farve.
sentence.en: I like the chair's design and color.

desperat.explanation: "Desperat" means "desperate". To say what a person is desperate to get, use "efter" (for): "Hun er desperat efter et job" (She is desperate for a job).

sentence.da: Han var **desperat** og ringede til alle.
sentence.en: He was desperate and called everyone.

desto.explanation: "Desto" means "the" in a pair like "the more..., the better". It comes in the second half, after "jo" (the) in the first: "Jo mere du øver, desto bedre bliver du" (The more you practice, the better you get).

sentence.da: Jo ældre vinen er, **desto** dyrere bliver den.
sentence.en: The older the wine is, the more expensive it gets.

desuden.explanation: "Desuden" means "besides". To add one more point after a reason: "Huset er for dyrt. Desuden ligger det langt væk." (The house is too expensive. Besides, it is far away.)

sentence.da: Jeg er træt, og **desuden** er det sent.
sentence.en: I am tired, and besides, it is late.

desværre.explanation: "Desværre" means "unfortunately". To tell someone bad news: "Desværre er butikken lukket" (Unfortunately the shop is closed).

sentence.da: **Desværre** har jeg ikke tid i dag.
sentence.en: Unfortunately, I do not have time today.

det.explanation: "Det" means "it". It stands for a thing that takes "et": "Jeg har et hus, og det er stort" (I have a house, and it is big). Things that take "en" use "den": "Jeg har en bil, og den er stor" (I have a car, and it is big). When you point to something just said or done, it means "that": "Det er sjovt" (That is fun). When there is no particular thing, such as weather: "Det regner" (It is raining).

forms.en: I know it / I know that.

sentence.da: Se på huset! **Det** er meget gammelt.
sentence.en: Look at the house! It is very old.

det er.explanation: "Det er" means "it is". To name or describe a thing: "Det er en bog" (It is a book). To point at someone and say who they are, it means "that is": "Det er min bror" (That is my brother).

sentence.da: **Det er** en god dag i dag.
sentence.en: It is a good day today.

det er en god idé.explanation: "Det er en god idé" means "That's a good idea". To agree with a suggestion: "Skal vi gå en tur?" "Det er en god idé." (Shall we go for a walk? That's a good idea.) The short form is "God idé!" (Good idea!).

sentence.da: Café i dag? **Det er en god idé.**
sentence.en: Cafe today? That's a good idea.

det er fint med mig.explanation: "Det er fint med mig" means "that's fine with me" and agrees to a plan. Change "mig" (me) to "dig" (you) to ask: "Er det fint med dig?" (Is that fine with you?).

forms.da: Ja, det er fint med mig.
Hvis det er fint med dig.

sentence.da: Vi ses klokken fem? **Det er fint med mig.**
sentence.en: See you at five? That's fine with me.

det er hip som hap.explanation: "Det er hip som hap" means "It's all the same". To say you do not mind which option is chosen: "Kaffe eller te?" "Det er hip som hap." (Coffee or tea? Either is fine.)

forms.da: Det er hip som hap, hvad vi vælger
forms.en: It's all the same what we choose

forms.da: Det er hip som hap, om vi går nu eller senere
forms.en: It makes no difference whether we go now or later

sentence.da: **Det er hip som hap**, fordi bussen og toget koster det samme.
sentence.en: It's all the same, because the bus and the train cost the same.

det er i orden.explanation: "Det er i orden" means "It's okay". To agree to a plan: "Vi ses klokken otte?" "Det er i orden." (See you at eight? That's fine.) Literally, "i orden" means "in order".

sentence.da: Undskyld! — **Det er i orden.**
sentence.en: Sorry! — It's okay.

det er ikke så svært.explanation: "Det er ikke så svært" means "It's not that hard". It is built from "svært" (difficult) and "ikke så" (not so). To reassure someone who is stuck: "Jeg kan ikke finde ud af det." "Det er ikke så svært." (I cannot figure it out. It's not that hard.)

sentence.da: Dansk? **Det er ikke så svært.**
sentence.en: Danish? It's not that hard.

det er lige det.explanation: "Det er lige det" means "Yes, that's exactly it". To confirm that someone has understood you: "Du mener, at vi skal vente?" "Det er lige det." (You mean we should wait? That's exactly it.) Said short, "lige det" means "exactly that": "Jeg ville have lige det" (I wanted exactly that).

forms.da: Det er lige det, jeg mener
Nej, det er ikke lige det

sentence.da: Præcis, **det er lige det**, jeg mener.
sentence.en: Exactly, that's just what I mean.

det er lige meget.explanation: "Det er lige meget" means "It doesn't matter". To say you do not mind which option is chosen: "Pizza eller pasta?" "Det er lige meget." (Pizza or pasta? It doesn't matter.) To say "I don't care", add "mig" (me): "Det er mig lige meget". This can sound rude.

forms.da: Det er lige meget, hvad du vælger.
forms.en: It doesn't matter what you choose.

sentence.da: Te eller kaffe? **Det er lige meget.**
sentence.en: Tea or coffee? It doesn't matter.

det er min skyld.explanation: "Det er min skyld" means "It's my fault". To blame someone else, change "min" (my) to "hans" (his): "Det er hans skyld" (It's his fault).

sentence.da: Jeg glemte at ringe, **det er min skyld**.
sentence.en: I forgot to call, it's my fault.

det er rigtigt.explanation: "Det er rigtigt" means "That's right". To agree that something is correct: "Er mødet klokken ti?" "Ja, det er rigtigt." (Is the meeting at ten? Yes, that's right.) A mix-up: "rigtig" before another word means "really", as in "rigtig godt" (really good).

sentence.da: Du bor i Aarhus? **Det er rigtigt.**
sentence.en: You live in Aarhus? That's right.

det er synd.explanation: "Det er synd" means "That's a shame". To answer bad news: "Hun er syg i dag." "Åh, det er synd." (She is sick today. Oh, that's a shame.) To name the person you feel sorry for, add "for" (for): "Det er synd for dig" (That's too bad for you).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke komme? **Det er synd!**
sentence.en: You can't come? That's a shame!

det giver ikke mening.explanation: "Det giver ikke mening" means "that doesn't make sense". Word for word, it means "that gives no meaning". To say it makes no sense at all, add "slet" (at all): "Det giver slet ikke mening" (That makes no sense at all).

forms.en: That makes no sense at all

sentence.da: Du siger ja og nej, og **det giver ikke mening**.
sentence.en: You say yes and no, and that doesn't make sense.

det giver mening.explanation: "Det giver mening" means "that makes sense". The word "mening" (meaning, sense) also means "opinion": "Hvad er din mening?" (What is your opinion?).

sentence.da: Nu forstår jeg, og **det giver mening**.
sentence.en: Now I understand, and that makes sense.

det går fint.explanation: "Det går fint" means "it's going fine". When someone asks how you are, you can answer: "Hvordan går det?" "Det går fint." (How is it going? It's going fine.) To say things are going badly, swap "fint" (fine) for "dårligt" (badly): "Det går dårligt" (It's going badly).

sentence.da: Hvordan går det? **Det går fint.**
sentence.en: How is it going? It's going fine.

det går godt.explanation: "Det går godt" means "it's going well". When someone asks "Hvordan går det?" (How is it going?), you can answer "Det går godt." To ask the same question back, add "og dig?" (and you?): "Det går godt, og dig?" (I'm doing well, and you?)

sentence.da: Hvordan går det? **Det går godt.**
sentence.en: How is it going? It's going well.

det gør ikke noget.explanation: "Det gør ikke noget" means "it's okay". You say it when someone says "Undskyld" (Sorry): "Undskyld, jeg kom for sent." "Det gør ikke noget." (Sorry, I was late. It's okay.) Word for word, it means "it does not do anything". Do not mix it up with "det er lige meget" (it does not matter). You say that one when two options are equally fine to you: "Te eller kaffe?" "Det er lige meget." (Tea or coffee? It does not matter.)

forms.da: Det gør ikke noget, jeg venter.

sentence.da: "Undskyld!" – "**Det gør ikke noget.**"
sentence.en: "Sorry!" – "It's okay."

det håber jeg.explanation: "Det håber jeg" means "I hope so". To answer a question about something that may happen, say: "Kommer Anna i morgen?" "Det håber jeg." (Is Anna coming tomorrow? I hope so.) Word for word, it means "that hope I".

sentence.da: Bliver det godt vejr? **Det håber jeg.**
sentence.en: Will the weather be good? I hope so.

det kan godt være.explanation: "Det kan godt være" means "that may be". To agree that the other person could be right and then give your own view, add "men" (but): "Det er for dyrt." "Det kan godt være, men jeg vil have den." (It is too expensive. That may be, but I want it.)

forms.da: Det kan godt være, du har ret.
forms.en: That may be, you could be right.

sentence.da: **Det kan godt være**, men jeg ser det anderledes.
sentence.en: That may be, but I see it differently.

det kan man ikke vide.explanation: "Det kan man ikke vide" means "you never know". To answer a question about the future, say: "Bliver det sol i morgen?" "Det kan man ikke vide." (Will it be sunny tomorrow? You never know.) Word for word, it means "that can one not know".

sentence.da: Måske bliver det godt. **Det kan man ikke vide**.
sentence.en: Maybe it will be good. You never know.

det kommer an på.explanation: "Det kommer an på" means "it depends". Say what it depends on right after "på" (on): "Det kommer an på vejret" (It depends on the weather).

sentence.da: **Det kommer an på**, hvor meget det koster.
sentence.en: It depends on how much it costs.

det lyder godt.explanation: "Det lyder godt" means "that sounds good". Say it when someone offers you something: "Vil du have en kop kaffe?" "Det lyder godt." (Would you like a cup of coffee? That sounds good.) "At lyde" means "to sound".

sentence.da: Middag klokken seks? **Det lyder godt.**
sentence.en: Dinner at six? That sounds good.

det passer.explanation: "Det passer" means "that's true" and confirms a fact. Add "ikke" (not) to say the opposite: "Det passer ikke" (That's not true).

sentence.da: Du er fra Norge, ikke? Ja, **det passer**.
sentence.en: You are from Norway, right? Yes, that's true.

det passer ikke.explanation: "Det passer ikke" means "that's not true". To correct a claim, say: "Du var der i går." "Det passer ikke." (You were there yesterday. That's not true.) To say a claim is true, leave out "ikke" (not): "Det passer" (That's true).

sentence.da: **Det passer ikke**, jeg var der ikke i går.
sentence.en: That's not true, I wasn't there yesterday.

det tror jeg.explanation: "Det tror jeg" means "I think so". To answer a question when you believe the answer is yes, say: "Kommer Anna i dag?" "Det tror jeg." (Is Anna coming today? I think so.) Word for word, it means "that believe I".

sentence.da: Er han hjemme? **Det tror jeg.**
sentence.en: Is he home? I think so.

det tror jeg ikke.explanation: "Det tror jeg ikke" means "I don't think so". To answer a question when you believe the answer is no, say: "Kommer Anna i dag?" "Det tror jeg ikke." (Is Anna coming today? I don't think so.) Word for word, it means "that believe I not".

sentence.da: Regner det i dag? **Det tror jeg ikke.**
sentence.en: Is it raining today? I don't think so.

det var dog utroligt.explanation: "Det var dog utroligt" means "that's incredible". When someone tells you surprising news, you can react: "Jeg vandt i lotto!" "Det var dog utroligt!" (I won the lottery! That's incredible!) The word "utroligt" is built from "u-" (un-) and "trolig" (likely).

sentence.da: Hun vandt tre gange i træk, **det var dog utroligt**!
sentence.en: She won three times in a row, that's incredible!

det var på høje tid.explanation: "Det var på høje tid" means "it was high time". To tell someone they came late, say: "Det var på høje tid, at du kom!" (It was high time you showed up!) Word for word, it means "it was on high time".

forms.da: Nu er det på høje tid at gå
forms.en: Now it is high time to go

sentence.da: Taget lækkede i årevis, og **det var på høje tid** at skifte det.
sentence.en: The roof leaked for years, and it was high time to replace it.

det var så lidt.explanation: "Det var så lidt" means "you're welcome". When someone thanks you, you can answer: "Tak, fordi du hjalp mig!" "Det var så lidt." (Thank you for helping me! You're welcome.) Word for word, it means "it was so little".

forms.da: Tak for hjælpen! – Det var så lidt.
forms.en: Thanks for the help! – Don't mention it.

sentence.da: Tak for hjælpen! **Det var så lidt.**
sentence.en: Thanks for the help! Don't mention it.

det ved jeg ikke.explanation: "Det ved jeg ikke" means "I don't know". Word for word, it means "that know I not". "At vide" (to know) is for facts. To say you know a person or place, use "at kende" (to be familiar with) instead: "Jeg kender Peter" (I know Peter).

forms.da: Det ved jeg ikke noget om.

sentence.da: Hvor er Peter? **Det ved jeg ikke.**
sentence.en: Where is Peter? I don't know.

det vil sige.explanation: "Det vil sige" means "that is to say". To explain or sum up what you just said, put it before the explanation: "Jeg bor i Jylland, det vil sige i Aarhus" (I live in Jutland, that is to say in Aarhus). Word for word, it means "that will say". The short form in writing is "dvs." (i.e.).

forms.da: Det vil sige, at du kommer
forms.en: That is to say, you are coming

sentence.da: Vi mødes klokken otte, **det vil sige** om en time.
sentence.en: We meet at eight, that is to say in an hour.

detaljeret.explanation: "Detaljeret" means "detailed". It comes from the noun "en detalje" (a detail). To describe an explanation that gives every detail, say: "en detaljeret beskrivelse" (a detailed description).

sentence.da: Kortet er meget **detaljeret**, og man kan se hver eneste sti.
sentence.en: The map is very detailed, and you can see every single path.

dets.explanation: "Dets" means "its". When the thing belongs to a word that takes "et", such as "et værelse" (a room), say: "dets vindue" (its window). When the thing belongs to a word that takes "en", such as "en bil" (a car), use "dens" (its) instead: "dens motor" (its engine).

sentence.da: Huset er gammelt, men **dets** tag er nyt.
sentence.en: The house is old, but its roof is new.

dette.explanation: "Dette" means "this" with a word that takes "et": "dette hus" (this house). With a word that takes "en", use "denne" (this): "denne bil" (this car). "Dette" sounds formal; in everyday speech Danes say "det her" (this one): "Jeg vil have det her" (I want this one).

sentence.da: Jeg vil købe **dette** hus.
sentence.en: I want to buy this house.

diabetes.explanation: "Diabetes" means "diabetes". It also appears in "svangerskabsdiabetes" (gestational diabetes), where "svangerskab" means "pregnancy".

sentence.da: Han har **diabetes** og tager insulin hver dag.
sentence.en: He has diabetes and takes insulin every day.

diarré.explanation: "Diarré" means "diarrhea". To spell it in Danish, end it with "é" with an accent, not with "a" as in English.

sentence.da: Man kan få **diarré** af dårlig mad.
sentence.en: You can get diarrhea from bad food.

diesel.explanation: "Diesel" means "diesel". To say you are filling the car with fuel, use "at tanke" (to fill up with fuel): "Jeg skal tanke diesel" (I need to fill up with diesel).

sentence.da: Varebilen kører på **diesel**, ikke på benzin.
sentence.en: The van runs on diesel, not on gasoline.

dig.explanation: "Dig" means "you". When you talk to one person who receives the action, use "dig": "Jeg ringer til dig" (I am calling you). When that person does the action, use "du" (you) instead: "Du ringer til mig" (You are calling me). To talk to several people, use "jer" (you, many): "Jeg ringer til jer" (I am calling you all).

sentence.da: Jeg kan høre **dig**.
sentence.en: I can hear you.

digital.explanation: "Digital" means "digital". To describe a word that takes "et", add "t": "et digitalt ur" (a digital watch). Before a plural word, add "e": "digitale ure" (digital watches).

sentence.da: Uret er **digital** og viser tiden med tal.
sentence.en: The watch is digital and shows the time with numbers.

dild.explanation: "Dild" means "dill". To tell someone to chop the herb, say: "Hak dilden fint" (Chop the dill finely).

sentence.da: Fisken smager godt med **dild**.
sentence.en: The fish tastes good with dill.

din.explanation: "Din" means "your". It goes with a word that takes "en", such as "en hat" (a hat): "din hat" (your hat). With a word that takes "et", say "dit": "dit værelse" (your room). Before more than one thing, say "dine": "dine nøgler" (your keys).

sentence.da: Her er **din** kaffe.
sentence.en: Here is your coffee.

dine.explanation: "Dine" means "your". Use it before more than one thing: "dine nøgler" (your keys). For one thing that takes "en", say "din": "din nøgle" (your key). For one thing that takes "et", say "dit": "dit hus" (your house).

sentence.da: Tag **dine** sko på.
sentence.en: Put your shoes on.

diplomatisk.explanation: "Diplomatisk" means "diplomatic". When you talk about how countries deal with each other, use it: "en diplomatisk krise" (a diplomatic crisis). When you want someone to handle a delicate situation with care, say: "Vær diplomatisk" (Be diplomatic).

sentence.da: Hun var **diplomatisk** og sagde det på en venlig måde.
sentence.en: She was diplomatic and said it in a friendly way.

direkte.explanation: "Direkte" means "straight". When you talk about a flight with no stop on the way, it means "direct": "et direkte fly" (a direct flight).

sentence.da: Jeg tager **direkte** hjem efter arbejde.
sentence.en: I go straight home after work.

disciplin.explanation: "En disciplin" means "a discipline". When you talk about self-control, say: "Hun har stor disciplin" (She has great discipline). When you talk about one event in a sport, say: "Længdespring er en disciplin" (The long jump is an event).

sentence.da: Hundrede meter er en **disciplin** ved de olympiske lege.
sentence.en: The hundred meters is an event at the Olympic Games.

diset.explanation: "Diset" means "hazy". It comes from the noun "en dis" (a haze). To say the weather is hazy, say: "Det er diset i dag" (It is hazy today).

sentence.da: Morgenen var **diset**, og vi kunne næsten ikke se bjergene.
sentence.en: The morning was hazy, and we could hardly see the mountains.

diskret.explanation: "Diskret" means "discreet". To ask someone to keep something private, say: "Vær diskret" (Be discreet). When you describe a quiet style that does not stand out, it means "subtle": "en diskret farve" (a subtle color).

sentence.da: Hun er **diskret** og fortæller aldrig andres hemmeligheder.
sentence.en: She is discreet and never tells other people's secrets.

diskrimination.explanation: "Diskrimination" means "discrimination". To say the reason, use "på grund af" (because of): "diskrimination på grund af alder" (discrimination because of age).

sentence.da: **Diskrimination** er, når nogen bliver behandlet dårligere på grund af deres køn.
sentence.en: Discrimination is when someone is treated worse because of their gender.

disse.explanation: "Disse" means "these". When you point to one thing instead of several, use "denne" (this) for a word that takes "en": "denne sko" (this shoe). For a word that takes "et", use "dette" (this): "dette hus" (this house). "Disse" is formal. In everyday speech, "de her" (these) is the plain way to say it: "de her sko" (these shoes).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide **disse** sko.
sentence.en: I like these shoes.

distraheret.explanation: "Distraheret" means "distracted". To name what distracts you, add "af" (by): "Jeg var distraheret af min telefon" (I was distracted by my phone).

sentence.da: Jeg er **distraheret**, fordi der er så meget støj.
sentence.en: I am distracted because there is so much noise.

dit.explanation: "Dit" means "your". It goes with a word that takes "et", such as "et værelse" (a room): "dit værelse" (your room). With a word that takes "en", say "din": "din bil" (your car). Before more than one thing, say "dine": "dine sko" (your shoes).

sentence.da: Hvad er **dit** navn?
sentence.en: What is your name?

dna.explanation: "DNA" means "DNA". It takes "et", as the form "DNA'et" (the DNA) shows. To say the police found it somewhere, say: "Politiet fandt DNA på stedet" (The police found DNA at the scene).

sentence.da: **DNA** gør, at børn ligner deres forældre.
sentence.en: DNA makes children look like their parents.

dobbelt.explanation: "Dobbelt" means "double". To compare two ages, say: "Han er dobbelt så gammel som mig" (He is twice as old as me). It is also the first part of other words, such as "dobbeltværelse" (double room).

sentence.da: Det koster **dobbelt** så meget i byen.
sentence.en: It costs twice as much in the city.

dog.explanation: "Dog" means "though". When you want to say "all the same", use it: "Det er dyrt, men jeg køber det dog" (It is expensive, but I am buying it anyway). When you want to make an invitation or request friendlier, use it: "Sæt dig dog" (Do sit down).

sentence.da: Kom **dog** ind, Peter!
sentence.en: Do come in, Peter!

dokumentation.explanation: "Dokumentation" means "documentation". To say what the documentation belongs to, add "til" (for): "dokumentationen til programmet" (the documentation for the program).

sentence.da: Kvitteringer er **dokumentation** for, hvad man har købt.
sentence.en: Receipts are documentation of what you have bought.

dommedag.explanation: "Dommedag" means "doomsday". It is built from "en dom" (a verdict) and "en dag" (a day). To say that something is not a disaster, say: "Det er ikke dommedag" (It is not the end of the world).

sentence.da: Ifølge kristendommen kommer **dommedag**, når Gud dømmer alle mennesker.
sentence.en: According to Christianity, Judgment Day comes when God judges all people.

doven.explanation: "Doven" means "lazy". To say how you feel today, say: "Jeg er doven i dag" (I am lazy today). The opposite is "flittig" (diligent): "Hun er flittig" (She is diligent).

sentence.da: Han er **doven** og ligger i sofaen hele dagen.
sentence.en: He is lazy and lies on the sofa all day.

dramatisk.explanation: "Dramatisk" means "dramatic". When you say that a person makes too much of things, say: "Du er så dramatisk!" (You are so dramatic!)

sentence.da: Det var en **dramatisk** redning, og alle holdt vejret.
sentence.en: It was a dramatic rescue, and everyone held their breath.

dressing.explanation: "En dressing" means "a dressing". To say what is in it, add "med" (with): "en dressing med hvidløg" (a dressing with garlic).

sentence.da: Jeg laver en **dressing** til salaten.
sentence.en: I make a dressing for the salad.

drikkepenge.explanation: "Drikkepenge" means "tip". Literally, it means "drink money", from "at drikke" (to drink) and "penge" (money). The word is used without an article. To tell a waiter to keep the change, say: "Tak, behold resten som drikkepenge" (Thanks, keep the change as a tip).

sentence.da: Vi gav tjeneren **drikkepenge**, fordi maden var god.
sentence.en: We gave the waiter a tip because the food was good.

drikkevarer.explanation: "Drikkevarer" means "drinks". It is built from "at drikke" (to drink) and "varer" (goods). To talk about one single drink, say "en drik" (a drink): "en kold drik" (a cold drink).

sentence.da: Vi sælger mad og **drikkevarer** i kiosken.
sentence.en: We sell food and drinks in the kiosk.

dristig.explanation: "Dristig" means "bold". When you describe clothes that dare to be different, it means "daring": "en dristig kjole" (a daring dress).

sentence.da: En **dristig** person tør tage chancer, som andre ikke tør.
sentence.en: A bold person dares to take chances that others do not dare to.

du.explanation: "Du" means "you". When you talk to one person, say: "Er du træt?" (Are you tired?) Danes use "du" with older people and with a boss too. When that person receives the action, use "dig" (you): "Jeg ser dig" (I see you). To talk to several people, say "I" (you, many): "I er søde" (You are all sweet).

sentence.da: Hvor bor **du**?
sentence.en: Where do you live?

dug.explanation: "En dug" means "dew". When you talk about a cloth on a table, "en dug" is a different word: "en hvid dug" (a white tablecloth).

sentence.da: Om morgenen ligger der **dug** på græsset.
sentence.en: In the morning there is dew on the grass.

dum.explanation: "Dum" means "stupid". When you say it about a person, it sounds rude: "Du er dum" (You are stupid). To say a thing was stupid, add "t": "Det var dumt" (That was stupid).

sentence.da: Det var en **dum** fejl.
sentence.en: That was a stupid mistake.

dyb.explanation: "Dyb" means "deep". When you talk about sleep, use it: "en dyb søvn" (a deep sleep). When you talk about a voice, use it too: "en dyb stemme" (a deep voice).

sentence.da: Søen er for **dyb** til børn.
sentence.en: The lake is too deep for children.

dybtgående.explanation: "Dybtgående" means "thorough". It is built from "dybt" (deeply) and "gående" (going). When you talk about changes that go far, it means "profound": "dybtgående reformer" (profound reforms).

sentence.da: En **dybtgående** undersøgelse tager lang tid, men den finder de skjulte fejl.
sentence.en: A thorough investigation takes a long time, but it finds the hidden errors.

dygtig.explanation: "Dygtig" means "skilled". To name the skill, add "til" (at): "dygtig til sprog" (good at languages). To praise someone, say "Dygtig!" (Well done!)

sentence.da: Han er **dygtig** og lærer hurtigt.
sentence.en: He is capable and learns quickly.

dynamisk.explanation: "Dynamisk" means "dynamic". It comes from the noun "en dynamik" (dynamics). To describe a city that keeps changing, say: "en dynamisk by" (a dynamic city).

sentence.da: Firmaet er **dynamisk** og ændrer sig hele tiden.
sentence.en: The company is dynamic and keeps changing all the time.

dyr.explanation: "Dyr" means "expensive". Do not mix it up with "et dyr" (an animal): "Hunden er et dyr" (The dog is an animal), "Hunden er dyr" (The dog is expensive).

sentence.da: Jakken koster 5000 kroner. Den er meget **dyr**.
sentence.en: The jacket costs 5000 kroner. It is very expensive.

dyrebar.explanation: "Dyrebar" means "precious". It comes from the word "dyr" (expensive). To say that time is precious, say: "Tid er dyrebar" (Time is precious).

sentence.da: Mormors gamle ring er **dyrebar** for mig.
sentence.en: Grandma's old ring is precious to me.

dyrevelfærd.explanation: "Dyrevelfærd" means "animal welfare". It is built from "et dyr" (an animal) and "velfærd" (welfare). To talk about farms, say: "dyrevelfærd i landbruget" (animal welfare in farming).

sentence.da: God **dyrevelfærd** betyder, at dyrene har plads og får mad.
sentence.en: Good animal welfare means that the animals have room and get food.

dårlig.explanation: "Dårlig" means "bad". To say how you feel, use "dårligt" with "have det" (to feel): "Jeg har det dårligt" (I feel bad). "Dårlig" has its own words for "worse" and "worst": "værre" (worse) and "værst" (worst).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og har en **dårlig** dag.
sentence.en: I am sick and having a bad day.

dårlig til.explanation: "Dårlig til" means "bad at". It is built from "dårlig" (bad) and "til" (at). To ask someone what they are bad at, say: "Hvad er du dårlig til?" (What are you bad at?)

forms.da: Jeg er dårlig til at lave mad.
Vi er dårlige til at danse.

sentence.da: Han er **dårlig til** at svømme, men han prøver.
sentence.en: He is bad at swimming, but he tries.

død.explanation: "Død" means "dead". When you talk about a device that has stopped working, use it too: "Min telefon er død" (My phone is dead).

sentence.da: Blomsten er **død** uden vand.
sentence.en: The flower is dead without water.

dødbringende.explanation: "Dødbringende" means "deadly". It is built from "død" (death) and "bringende" (bringing). To talk about a danger, say: "et dødbringende virus" (a deadly virus). To say that people can die, use "dødelig" (mortal) instead: "Vi er alle dødelige" (We are all mortal).

sentence.da: Slangens bid er **dødbringende**, når man ikke får modgift hurtigt.
sentence.en: The snake's bite is deadly when you do not get an antidote quickly.

dødelig.explanation: "Dødelig" means "deadly". When you talk about something that can kill, use it: "Svampen er dødelig" (The mushroom is deadly). When you talk about people who can die, it means "mortal": "Vi er alle dødelige" (We are all mortal).

sentence.da: Giften fra slangen er **dødelig** for mennesker.
sentence.en: The venom from the snake is deadly to humans.

dødkedelig.explanation: "Dødkedelig" means "deadly boring". It is built from "død" (dead) and "kedelig" (boring). The same "død-" in front of another word makes it extreme, as in "dødtræt" (dead tired).

sentence.da: Filmen var **dødkedelig**, og jeg faldt i søvn.
sentence.en: The movie was deadly boring, and I fell asleep.

dødsstraf.explanation: "En dødsstraf" means "a death penalty". It is built from "en død" (a death) and "en straf" (a punishment). To say a court gives it, use "at idømme" (to impose): "Retten idømte ham dødsstraf" (The court imposed the death penalty on him).

sentence.da: **Dødsstraf** er den hårdeste straf, en stat kan give.
sentence.en: The death penalty is the harshest punishment a state can give.

dømmekraft.explanation: "En dømmekraft" means "a judgment", as in good sense and not a court decision. It is built from "at dømme" (to judge) and "kraft" (power). To say a task needs good sense, say: "Det kræver dømmekraft" (It takes judgment).

sentence.da: Når man har **dømmekraft**, tænker man sig om, før man beslutter noget.
sentence.en: When you have judgment, you think before you decide anything.

døv.explanation: "Døv" means "deaf". To say someone hears a little, use "hørehæmmet" (hard of hearing) instead: "Min far er hørehæmmet" (My father is hard of hearing).

sentence.da: Hun er født **døv** og taler med hænderne.
sentence.en: She was born deaf and talks with her hands.

en dag.explanation: "En dag" means "a day". To say every day, use "hver dag" (every day). To greet someone, say "god dag" (hello). The names of the days of the week end in "-dag", such as "mandag" (Monday) and "tirsdag" (Tuesday).

sentence.da: Mandag er den første **dag** i ugen.
sentence.en: Monday is the first day of the week.

en dagbog.explanation: "En dagbog" means "a diary". It is built from "dag" (day) and "bog" (book). To say you write a diary, use "at føre dagbog" (to keep a diary).

sentence.da: Hun skriver hver aften i sin **dagbog**.
sentence.en: She writes in her diary every evening.

en daglig leder.explanation: "En daglig leder" means "a general manager". Literally, it means "a daily leader". To ask who runs the place, say: "Hvem er den daglige leder?" (Who is the general manager?)

sentence.da: Han er både ejer og **daglig leder** af butikken.
sentence.en: He is both the owner and general manager of the shop.

en dagligvare.explanation: "En dagligvare" means "a grocery item". It is built from "daglig" (daily) and "en vare" (a product). To talk about groceries in general, use the plural: "Jeg køber dagligvarer" (I buy groceries).

sentence.da: Mælk er en **dagligvare**, som vi køber hver uge.
sentence.en: Milk is a grocery item that we buy every week.

en dagplejer.explanation: "En dagplejer" means "a home daycare provider". In Denmark, parents can choose one for the youngest children instead of "en vuggestue" (a daycare center for toddlers): "Vores datter går i vuggestue" (Our daughter goes to a daycare center).

sentence.da: Vores søn er hos en **dagplejer**, mens vi arbejder.
sentence.en: Our son is with a home daycare provider while we work.

en dagsorden.explanation: "En dagsorden" means "an agenda". It is built from "dag" (day) and "en orden" (an order). When you talk about topics that society is discussing, say: "noget er på dagsordenen" (something is on the agenda).

sentence.da: Før mødet sender lederen en **dagsorden** til alle.
sentence.en: Before the meeting, the manager sends an agenda to everyone.

en dagsrejse.explanation: "En dagsrejse" means "a day trip". It is built from "dag" (day) and "rejse" (journey). To say where the trip goes, add "til" (to): "en dagsrejse til Skagen" (a day trip to Skagen).

sentence.da: Vi tager på en **dagsrejse** og er hjemme i aften.
sentence.en: We go on a day trip and are home tonight.

en dal.explanation: "En dal" means "a valley". To say where a valley lies, say: "en dal mellem bjergene" (a valley between the mountains).

sentence.da: Floden løber gennem en smuk **dal**.
sentence.en: The river runs through a beautiful valley.

en dam.explanation: "En dam" means "a pond". To talk about a larger body of water, use "en sø" (a lake): "Vi svømmer i søen" (We swim in the lake).

sentence.da: Der bor mange frøer i den lille **dam**.
sentence.en: Many frogs live in the little pond.

en dame.explanation: "En dame" means "a lady". To mark the women's restroom, a door says "Damer" (ladies). To greet an audience, say: "Mine damer og herrer" (Ladies and gentlemen).

sentence.da: En pige bliver til en **dame**.
sentence.en: A girl becomes a lady.

en dannelse.explanation: "En dannelse" means "an education", as in good manners and wide knowledge. To talk about school or job training, use "en uddannelse" (a training program) instead: "Jeg tager en uddannelse som elektriker" (I am training as an electrician). When you talk about how something comes into being, "dannelse" means "formation": "dannelsen af skyer" (the formation of clouds).

sentence.da: **Dannelse** handler om manerer og viden, ikke om eksamener.
sentence.en: Cultural education is about manners and knowledge, not about exams.

en dans.explanation: "En dans" means "a dance". It comes from the verb "at danse" (to dance). To ask someone to dance, say: "Må jeg få denne dans?" (May I have this dance?)

sentence.da: Jeg har lært en ny **dans** til festen.
sentence.en: I have learned a new dance for the party.

en danser.explanation: "En danser" means "a dancer". To say what someone does for a living, leave out "en": "Hun er danser" (She is a dancer).

sentence.da: Hun er en god **danser**, og hun øver hver dag.
sentence.en: She is a good dancer, and she practices every day.

en dansker.explanation: "En dansker" means "a Dane". To ask about someone's nationality, leave out "en": "Er du dansker?" (Are you a Dane?) For the language, use "dansk" (Danish): "Jeg taler dansk" (I speak Danish).

sentence.da: Han bor i Danmark og er **dansker**.
sentence.en: He lives in Denmark and is a Dane.

en danskuddannelse.explanation: "En danskuddannelse" means "a Danish course (for adults)", the official Danish teaching for foreigners who live in Denmark. It comes in three levels, called "danskuddannelse 1", "2" and "3", and the level depends on how much schooling the learner had before.

sentence.da: Hun tager en **danskuddannelse** på sprogcentret to gange om ugen.
sentence.en: She takes a Danish course at the language center twice a week.

en dataanalytiker.explanation: "En dataanalytiker" means "a data analyst". To say what your job is, leave out "en": "Jeg er dataanalytiker" (I am a data analyst).

sentence.da: En **dataanalytiker** undersøger tal for at finde mønstre.
sentence.en: A data analyst examines numbers to find patterns.

en database.explanation: "En database" means "a database". To say you look something up in it, say: "Jeg søger i databasen" (I am searching the database).

sentence.da: Vi gemmer alle navne i en **database**.
sentence.en: We save all the names in a database.

en date.explanation: "En date" means "a date", as in a romantic meeting. The word is borrowed from English. For a date on the calendar, use "en dato" (a calendar date): "Hvilken dato er det?" (What date is it?)

sentence.da: Han har en **date** i aften og er meget nervøs.
sentence.en: He has a date tonight and is very nervous.

en dato.explanation: "En dato" means "a date (calendar)", such as 5 March. Do not mix it up with "en date" (a romantic meeting), which is borrowed from English: "Hun har en date i aften" (She has a date tonight).

sentence.da: Hvilken **dato** er det i dag?
sentence.en: What date is it today?

en datter.explanation: "En datter" means "a daughter". To say "my daughter", use "min": "Min datter er syv år" (My daughter is seven years old).

sentence.da: Jeg har en søn og en **datter**.
sentence.en: I have a son and a daughter.

en deadline.explanation: "En deadline" means "a deadline". The word is borrowed from English. A Danish word for the same thing is "en frist" (a time limit): "Fristen er fredag" (The deadline is Friday).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **deadline** på fredag.
sentence.en: I have a deadline on Friday.

en debat.explanation: "En debat" means "a debate". To say you take part in one, use "at deltage i" (to take part in): "Hun deltager i debatten" (She takes part in the debate).

sentence.da: Der var en lang **debat** om skolen i fjernsynet i går.
sentence.en: There was a long debate about the school on TV yesterday.

en debattør.explanation: "En debattør" means "a debater". It is built from "en debat" (a debate). To say what someone is, leave out "en": "Hun er debattør" (She is a debater).

sentence.da: Som kendt **debattør** skriver hun ofte om politik i aviserne.
sentence.en: As a well-known debater, she often writes about politics in the newspapers.

en debut.explanation: "En debut" means "a debut". The matching verb is "at debutere" (to make your debut): "Hun debuterede som forfatter i 2010" (She made her debut as a writer in 2010).

sentence.da: Hendes **debut** som forfatter var en roman om barndommen.
sentence.en: Her debut as a writer was a novel about childhood.

en deciliter.explanation: "En deciliter" means "a deciliter". In writing, it is shortened to "dl": "2 dl mel" (2 deciliters of flour).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger to **deciliter** mel i brødet.
sentence.en: I use two deciliters of flour in the bread.

en definition.explanation: "En definition" means "a definition". After "definition", use "på" (of) and then the word being defined: "Hvad er definitionen på frihed?" (What is the definition of freedom?)

sentence.da: Jeg kender ikke ordets **definition**.
sentence.en: I do not know the definition of the word.

en dej.explanation: "En dej" means "a dough". For pancake batter, the Danish word is also "dej": "pandekagedej" (pancake batter).

sentence.da: Jeg laver **dej** af mel og vand.
sentence.en: I make dough from flour and water.

en dekoration.explanation: "En dekoration" means "a decoration". The matching verb is "at dekorere" (to decorate): "Vi dekorerer stuen" (We are decorating the living room).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en **dekoration** til bordet.
sentence.en: I am buying a decoration for the table.

en del.explanation: "En del" means "a part". When you talk about how many people or things there are, it means "quite a lot": "Der er en del mennesker her" (There are quite a few people here).

sentence.da: Musik er en stor **del** af mit liv.
sentence.en: Music is a big part of my life.

en delfin.explanation: "En delfin" means "a dolphin". It is spelled with "e" and "f", not with "o" and "ph" as in English.

sentence.da: En **delfin** bor i havet og spiser fisk.
sentence.en: A dolphin lives in the sea and eats fish.

en delmængde.explanation: "En delmængde" means "a subset". It is built from "del" (part) and "en mængde" (a set).

sentence.da: Lige tal er en **delmængde** af de hele tal.
sentence.en: Even numbers are a subset of the whole numbers.

en deltager.explanation: "En deltager" means "a participant". It comes from the verb "at deltage" (to take part). To say which event someone took part in, use "i" (in) after it: "en deltager i kurset" (a participant in the course).

sentence.da: Hver **deltager** får en lille gave.
sentence.en: Each participant gets a small gift.

en deltagerliste.explanation: "En deltagerliste" means "a list of participants". It is built from "en deltager" (a participant) and "en liste" (a list). The part "liste" is also in "en indkøbsliste" (a shopping list).

sentence.da: Der er tyve navne på vores **deltagerliste**.
sentence.en: There are twenty names on our participant list.

en demonstration.explanation: "En demonstration" means "a demonstration". When a crowd gathers or marches to show publicly what it wants, use it for the event: "Der var en demonstration i går" (There was a demonstration yesterday). When someone shows how a machine works, use it for the showing: "Vi fik en demonstration af maskinen" (We were given a demonstration of the machine).

sentence.da: Tusindvis af mennesker gik til **demonstration** foran Christiansborg.
sentence.en: Thousands of people went to a demonstration in front of Christiansborg.

en deodorant.explanation: "En deodorant" means "a deodorant". To say you have or use deodorant in general, leave out "en": "Har du deodorant?" (Do you have deodorant?).

sentence.da: Jeg lugter ikke, fordi jeg bruger **deodorant**.
sentence.en: I do not smell bad, because I use deodorant.

en depression.explanation: "En depression" means "a depression". To describe a person who has one, use the adjective "deprimeret" (depressed): "Han er deprimeret" (He is depressed).

sentence.da: Når man har en **depression**, mister man ofte lysten til alt.
sentence.en: When you have depression, you often lose interest in everything.

en designer.explanation: "En designer" means "a designer". To say what kind of designer someone is, put a word before it: "en grafisk designer" (a graphic designer).

sentence.da: Hun er **designer** og laver smukt tøj.
sentence.en: She is a designer and makes beautiful clothes.

en dessert.explanation: "En dessert" means "a dessert". To ask what the dessert will be, use "til" (for): "Hvad skal vi have til dessert?" (What are we having for dessert?). Do not mix it up with "en ørken" (a desert): "Sahara er en ørken" (The Sahara is a desert).

sentence.da: Efter maden vil jeg have en **dessert**.
sentence.en: After the meal I want a dessert.

en destination.explanation: "En destination" means "a destination". To say you arrive there, use "at nå" (to reach) before it: "Vi nåede vores destination sent om aftenen" (We reached our destination late in the evening).

sentence.da: Vores **destination** er en lille by ved havet.
sentence.en: Our destination is a small town by the sea.

en detalje.explanation: "En detalje" means "a detail". To say you do something in full detail, use "i detaljer" (in detail) after the verb: "Hun forklarede alt i detaljer" (She explained everything in detail).

sentence.da: Billedet er flot, men én **detalje** er forkert.
sentence.en: The picture is nice, but one detail is wrong.

en detektiv.explanation: "En detektiv" means "a detective". To talk about a detective who works for private clients, add "privat" at the start: "en privatdetektiv" (a private detective).

sentence.da: En **detektiv** leder efter spor på gerningsstedet.
sentence.en: A detective looks for clues at the crime scene.

en detektor.explanation: "En detektor" means "a detector". To name a detector for one kind of thing, put that thing before it: "en metaldetektor" (a metal detector). Do not mix it up with "en detektiv" (a detective): "Detektiven fandt nøglen" (The detective found the key).

sentence.da: En **detektor** i loftet giver alarm, hvis der er røg.
sentence.en: A detector in the ceiling sounds the alarm if there is smoke.

en diagnose.explanation: "En diagnose" means "a diagnosis". To say a doctor makes one, use "at stille" (to put) before it: "Lægen stillede en diagnose" (The doctor made a diagnosis).

sentence.da: Når man har fået en **diagnose**, kan lægen vælge en behandling.
sentence.en: Once you have a diagnosis, the doctor can choose a treatment.
