en dialekt.explanation: "En dialekt" means "a dialect". Denmark has regional dialects such as "sønderjysk" (the dialect of South Jutland) and "bornholmsk" (the dialect of Bornholm).

sentence.da: Mormor taler en **dialekt**, som jeg næsten ikke forstår.
sentence.en: Grandma speaks a dialect that I hardly understand.

en dialog.explanation: "En dialog" means "a dialogue". English speakers should note the spelling: Danish has no "ue" at the end. To say two sides talk openly with each other, use "at føre" (to hold): "Politikerne vil føre en dialog med borgerne" (The politicians want to hold a dialogue with the citizens).

sentence.da: Der er meget **dialog** og lidt handling i stykket.
sentence.en: There is a lot of dialogue and little action in the play.

en diamant.explanation: "En diamant" means "a diamond". To talk about jewelry, use the compound "en diamantring" (a diamond ring). In a card game, the suit is called "ruder" (diamonds) instead: "Hun har ruder es" (She has the ace of diamonds).

sentence.da: En **diamant** er så hård, at den kan skære i glas.
sentence.en: A diamond is so hard that it can cut glass.

en diameter.explanation: "En diameter" means "a diameter". Do not mix it up with "en radius" (a radius), which is half as long: "Cirklen har en radius på fem centimeter, så diameteren er ti" (The circle has a radius of five centimeters, so the diameter is ten).

sentence.da: Pizzaen har en **diameter** på tredive centimeter.
sentence.en: The pizza has a diameter of thirty centimeters.

en digter.explanation: "En digter" means "a poet". It comes from the verb "at digte" (to write poetry): "Han digter om natten" (He writes poetry at night).

sentence.da: En **digter** skriver digte om kærlighed, natur og livet.
sentence.en: A poet writes poems about love, nature and life.

en digtsamling.explanation: "En digtsamling" means "a poetry collection". It is built from "et digt" (a poem) and "en samling" (a collection). The part "samling" is also in "en frimærkesamling" (a stamp collection).

sentence.da: I en **digtsamling** står der mange digte af samme digter.
sentence.en: In a poetry collection there are many poems by the same poet.

en diktat.explanation: "En diktat" means "a dictation". It comes from the verb "at diktere" (to dictate): "Chefen dikterer et brev" (The boss dictates a letter).

sentence.da: Til **diktat** skriver eleverne ned, hvad læreren læser højt.
sentence.en: In dictation the students write down what the teacher reads aloud.

en diktator.explanation: "En diktator" means "a dictator". To name the kind of country he rules, use "et diktatur" (a dictatorship): "Landet er et diktatur" (The country is a dictatorship).

sentence.da: I et land med en **diktator** er der ingen frie valg.
sentence.en: In a country with a dictator there are no free elections.

en dimension.explanation: "En dimension" means "a dimension". To talk about space, use "i tre dimensioner" (in three dimensions): "et billede i tre dimensioner" (a picture in three dimensions). To say something adds a new side to a matter, use it as well: "Det giver sagen en ny dimension" (That gives the matter a new dimension).

sentence.da: Længde er en **dimension**, ligesom bredde og højde.
sentence.en: Length is a dimension, just like width and height.

en diplomat.explanation: "En diplomat" means "a diplomat". To describe a tactful person in daily life, use it too: "Hun er en rigtig diplomat" (She is a real diplomat). The adjective is "diplomatisk" (diplomatic): "Det var et diplomatisk svar" (That was a diplomatic answer).

sentence.da: Som **diplomat** bor han i udlandet og taler for sit land.
sentence.en: As a diplomat, he lives abroad and speaks for his country.

en direktør.explanation: "En direktør" means "a director or CEO". To say CEO precisely, add "administrerende" (managing): "Hun er administrerende direktør i et stort firma" (She is the managing director of a large company).

sentence.da: Firmaets **direktør** er chef for alle de ansatte.
sentence.en: The company's director is the boss of all the employees.

en dirigent.explanation: "En dirigent" means "a conductor". Do not mix it up with "en konduktør" (a ticket inspector on a train): "Konduktøren tjekker billetterne" (The ticket inspector checks the tickets). At a meeting, "en dirigent" is also the person who chairs it: "Vi skal vælge en dirigent til generalforsamlingen" (We need to choose a chair for the general meeting).

sentence.da: En **dirigent** viser orkestret, hvornår det skal spille højt.
sentence.en: A conductor shows the orchestra when to play loudly.

en disharmoni.explanation: "En disharmoni" means "a discord". It is built from "dis-" and "en harmoni" (a harmony), so it is the opposite. To say that notes in music clash, use it for the sound: "Akkorden var en disharmoni" (The chord was a discord).

sentence.da: Efter skænderiet var der **disharmoni** i hele familien.
sentence.en: After the quarrel, there was discord in the whole family.

en diskussion.explanation: "En diskussion" means "a discussion". It comes from the verb "at diskutere" (to discuss). To say what the topic is, use "om" (about) after it: "en diskussion om lønnen" (a discussion about the pay).

sentence.da: Vi havde en **diskussion** om, hvem der skulle betale.
sentence.en: We had a discussion about who should pay.

en diæt.explanation: "En diæt" means "a diet". To say you are on a diet, use "at holde" (to keep): "Jeg holder diæt" (I am on a diet). For the food you eat every day, use "kost" instead: "en sund kost" (a healthy diet).

sentence.da: Lægen anbefalede mig en **diæt** uden sukker.
sentence.en: The doctor recommended a sugar-free diet to me.

en djævel.explanation: "En djævel" means "a devil". To talk about a person you feel sorry for, use the phrase "en stakkels djævel" (a poor devil): "Han er en stakkels djævel" (He is a poor devil).

sentence.da: I mange billeder har en **djævel** horn og en lang hale.
sentence.en: In many pictures, a devil has horns and a long tail.

en doktor.explanation: "En doktor" means "a doctor". Do not mix it up with "en læge" (a medical doctor): "Jeg skal til lægen" (I am going to the doctor).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og skal til **doktor** Hansen.
sentence.en: I am sick and going to Doctor Hansen.

en dokumentar.explanation: "En dokumentar" means "a documentary". The full word is "en dokumentarfilm" (a documentary film). To say what a documentary is about, use "om" (about) after it: "Jeg har set en dokumentar om vikinger" (I have seen a documentary about the Vikings).

sentence.da: En **dokumentar** viser, hvordan pandaer lever i naturen.
sentence.en: A documentary shows how pandas live in the wild.

en dollar.explanation: "En dollar" means "a dollar". To ask a price in this currency, use "i dollar" (in dollars): "Hvad koster det i dollar?" (What does it cost in dollars?).

sentence.da: I USA betaler man med **dollar**.
sentence.en: In the USA you pay with dollars.

en dom.explanation: "En dom" means "a verdict". To say what punishment someone got, use it for the "sentence": "Han fik en dom på tre års fængsel" (He got a sentence of three years in prison).

sentence.da: Retten afsagde **dom** i sagen i går.
sentence.en: The court gave its verdict in the case yesterday.

en dommer.explanation: "En dommer" means "a judge". It comes from "en dom" (a verdict). To talk about the person who leads a football match, use it for the "referee": "Dommeren blæste i fløjten" (The referee blew the whistle).

sentence.da: I retten bestemmer en **dommer** straffen.
sentence.en: In court, a judge decides the punishment.

en domstol.explanation: "En domstol" means "a court". It is built from "en dom" (a verdict) and "en stol" (a chair). For a tennis or basketball court, use "en bane" (a court) instead: "Vi spiller tennis på banen" (We play tennis on the court).

sentence.da: Hvis man bryder loven, kan sagen komme for en **domstol**.
sentence.en: If you break the law, the case can go before a court.

en donut.explanation: "En donut" means "a donut". To say what it comes with, use "med" (with): "en donut med chokolade" (a donut with chocolate).

sentence.da: En **donut** er rund og har et hul i midten.
sentence.en: A donut is round and has a hole in the middle.

en dosis.explanation: "En dosis" means "a dose". To say how much of a medicine, put "af" (of) and the name after it: "en dosis medicin" (a dose of medicine). To say a small amount of something else, use it too: "en dosis humor" (a dose of humor).

sentence.da: Lægen siger, at jeg kun må tage én **dosis** om dagen.
sentence.en: The doctor says that I may only take one dose a day.

en drage.explanation: "En drage" means "a dragon or kite". When you talk about the fire-breathing creature in fairy tales, use it for the dragon: "Dragen spyr ild" (The dragon breathes fire). When you talk about a toy flown outdoors on a string, use it for the kite: "Jeg har en rød drage" (I have a red kite).

sentence.da: Børnene flyver med en **drage** på stranden.
sentence.en: The kids fly a kite on the beach.

en dragt.explanation: "En dragt" means "a suit or costume". When you talk about clothes for an important occasion, use it for the suit: "Hun tog en mørk dragt på" (She put on a dark suit). When you talk about dressing up as a character, use it for the costume: "en heksedragt" (a witch costume).

sentence.da: Hun har en blå **dragt** på til mødet.
sentence.en: She is wearing a blue suit to the meeting.

en dreng.explanation: "En dreng" means "a boy". The part "dreng" is also in "en drengestreg" (a boyish prank).

sentence.da: Den lille **dreng** leger med sin bil.
sentence.en: The little boy plays with his car.

en drik.explanation: "En drik" means "a drink". It comes from the verb "at drikke" (to drink). Do not mix it up with "en drink" (a cocktail): "Hun bestiller en drink i baren" (She orders a cocktail at the bar).

sentence.da: Vand er en sund **drik**.
sentence.en: Water is a healthy drink.

en drink.explanation: "En drink" means "a drink (cocktail)": "Vil du have en drink?" (Would you like a cocktail?) For a drink of any other kind, say "noget at drikke" (something to drink): "Vil du have noget at drikke?" (Would you like something to drink?).

sentence.da: Hun bestiller en **drink** i baren.
sentence.en: She orders a cocktail at the bar.

en drivhuseffekt.explanation: "En drivhuseffekt" means "a greenhouse effect". It is built from "et drivhus" (a greenhouse) and "en effekt" (an effect). The part "drivhus" is also in "drivhusgasser" (greenhouse gases).

sentence.da: Når gasserne holder på varmen, har vi en **drivhuseffekt**.
sentence.en: When the gases hold on to the heat, we have a greenhouse effect.

en drivkraft.explanation: "En drivkraft" means "a driving force". It is built from "driv-" (drive) and "en kraft" (a force). To say a person pushes a project forward, use it for that person: "Hun er drivkraften bag projektet" (She is the driving force behind the project).

sentence.da: Nysgerrighed er den vigtigste **drivkraft** for en forsker.
sentence.en: Curiosity is the most important driving force for a researcher.

en dronning.explanation: "En dronning" means "a queen". Before a name it works as a title: "dronning Margrethe" (Queen Margrethe).

sentence.da: En **dronning** har en krone på hovedet.
sentence.en: A queen has a crown on her head.

en dråbe.explanation: "En dråbe" means "a drop". To say there is none of something left, use it for a tiny amount: "Der er ikke en dråbe mælk tilbage" (There is not a drop of milk left). The phrase "en dråbe i havet" (a drop in the ocean) also exists: "Det er kun en dråbe i havet" (It is only a drop in the ocean).

sentence.da: Vandet drypper fra hanen, en **dråbe** ad gangen.
sentence.en: The water drips from the tap, one drop at a time.

en drøm.explanation: "En drøm" means "a dream". When you talk about what you see while you sleep, use it for the dream: "Jeg havde en mærkelig drøm i nat" (I had a strange dream last night). When you talk about what you wish for in life, use it for the wish: "Hendes drøm er at rejse jorden rundt" (Her dream is to travel around the world).

sentence.da: Min **drøm** er at bo ved havet.
sentence.en: My dream is to live by the sea.

en due.explanation: "En due" means "a pigeon or dove". To talk about the white bird that stands for peace, use "en fredsdue" (a peace dove): "Fredsduen er hvid" (The peace dove is white).

sentence.da: En **due** er en grå fugl i byen.
sentence.en: A pigeon is a gray bird in the city.

en duft.explanation: "En duft" means "a scent". Do not mix it up with "en lugt" (a smell), which can be bad: "Der er dårlig lugt her" (There is a bad smell here).

sentence.da: Der er en dejlig **duft** af kaffe i køkkenet.
sentence.en: There is a lovely scent of coffee in the kitchen.

en dug.explanation: "En dug" means "a tablecloth". To talk about the water that forms on grass in the morning, use the same word for dew: "Græsset er vådt af dug" (The grass is wet with dew).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger en hvid **dug** på bordet.
sentence.en: I put a white tablecloth on the table.

en dukke.explanation: "En dukke" means "a doll". To talk about a puppet, use the same word, as in "et dukketeater" (a puppet theater): "Børnene ser et dukketeater" (The children watch a puppet theater).

sentence.da: Pigen leger med sin **dukke**.
sentence.en: The girl is playing with her doll.

en dusør.explanation: "En dusør" means "a reward", as in money offered to whoever finds a lost thing or a wanted person. To say someone offers one, use "at udlove" (to offer publicly): "Politiet udlover en dusør" (The police offer a reward). Do not mix it up with "en belønning" (a reward for effort): "Hun fik en belønning for sit arbejde" (She got a reward for her work).

related.en: to put out a search notice

sentence.da: Familien har lovet en **dusør** til den, der finder katten.
sentence.en: The family has promised a bounty to whoever finds the cat.

en dværg.explanation: "En dværg" means "a dwarf". Before an animal's name, "dværg-" means a small kind: "en dværgkanin" (a dwarf rabbit).

sentence.da: Den lille **dværg** bor under bjerget og arbejder med guld.
sentence.en: The little dwarf lives under the mountain and works with gold.

en dybde.explanation: "En dybde" means "a depth". To talk about how far up something goes, use "en højde" (a height) instead: "Træet har en højde på ti meter" (The tree has a height of ten meters).

sentence.da: Søen har en **dybde** på ti meter.
sentence.en: The lake has a depth of ten meters.

en dyne.explanation: "En dyne" means "a duvet". To talk about the cover you put on it, use "et dynebetræk" (a duvet cover): "Jeg skifter dynebetræk" (I am changing the duvet cover). Do not mix it up with "et tæppe" (a blanket): "Jeg lægger et tæppe over mig i sofaen" (I put a blanket over myself on the sofa).

sentence.da: Om vinteren sover jeg under en tyk **dyne**.
sentence.en: In winter I sleep under a thick duvet.

en dyreart.explanation: "En dyreart" means "an animal species". It is built from "et dyr" (an animal) and "en art" (a species). To talk about plants, use "en plantart" (a plant species) instead.

sentence.da: Ulven er en **dyreart**, og ræven er en anden.
sentence.en: The wolf is an animal species, and the fox is another.

en dyrehandel.explanation: "En dyrehandel" means "a pet shop". It is built from "et dyr" (an animal) and "en handel" (a trade). The part "handel" is also in "en tøjhandel" (a clothing shop).

sentence.da: Vi købte en kanin og et bur i en **dyrehandel**.
sentence.en: We bought a rabbit and a cage in a pet shop.

en dyreven.explanation: "En dyreven" means "an animal lover". It is built from "et dyr" (an animal) and "en ven" (a friend), so literally it is "an animal friend". The part "dyr" is also in "et dyreliv" (wildlife).

sentence.da: Min onkel er en stor **dyreven** og har fem katte.
sentence.en: My uncle is a big animal lover and has five cats.

en dyrlæge.explanation: "En dyrlæge" means "a veterinarian". It is built from "et dyr" (an animal) and "en læge" (a doctor). The part "læge" is also in "en øjenlæge" (an eye doctor) and "en børnelæge" (a children's doctor). To say you take a pet to the vet, use "til" (to): "Jeg skal med katten til dyrlægen" (I am taking the cat to the vet).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til en **dyrlæge**, fordi min hund er syg.
sentence.en: I am calling a vet because my dog is sick.

en dåse.explanation: "En dåse" means "a can". To say what is inside, put the food right after it: "en dåse tomater" (a can of tomatoes). Do not mix it up with "et glas" (a glass jar): "et glas marmelade" (a jar of jam).

sentence.da: Man kan købe cola i en **dåse**.
sentence.en: You can buy cola in a can.

en dåseåbner.explanation: "En dåseåbner" means "a can opener". It is built from "en dåse" (a can) and "at åbne" (to open). The part "dåse" is also in "en dåseøl" (a canned beer).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke åbne dåsen uden en **dåseåbner**.
sentence.en: I cannot open the can without a can opener.

en dækning.explanation: "En dækning" means "a cover or coverage". To say an insurance policy pays for something, use it for the coverage: "Forsikringen giver dækning ved tyveri" (The insurance gives coverage in case of theft). To say people hide from danger, use "at gå i dækning" (to take cover): "Alle gik i dækning" (Everyone took cover).

sentence.da: Der er dårlig **dækning** i bjergene, så min telefon virker ikke.
sentence.en: There is poor coverage in the mountains, so my phone does not work.

en dæmon.explanation: "En dæmon" means "a demon". To talk about fears or bad habits a person struggles with, use "indre dæmoner" (inner demons): "Han kæmper med sine indre dæmoner" (He is fighting his inner demons).

sentence.da: I filmen skræmmer en **dæmon** familien, som bor i huset.
sentence.en: In the film, a demon frightens the family that lives in the house.

en dør.explanation: "En dør" means "a door": "Jeg lukker døren" (I close the door). Do not mix it up with the verb form "dør" of "at dø" (to die): "Blomsten dør" (The flower dies).

sentence.da: Man går ind i huset gennem en **dør**.
sentence.en: You go into the house through a door.

en dørkarm.explanation: "En dørkarm" means "a door frame". It is built from "en dør" (a door) and "en karm" (a frame). The part "dør" is also in "en dørklokke" (a doorbell) and "en dørmåtte" (a doormat).

sentence.da: Han slår hovedet i den lave **dørkarm**.
sentence.en: He hits his head on the low door frame.

en dørklokke.explanation: "En dørklokke" means "a doorbell". It is built from "en dør" (a door) and "en klokke" (a bell). The part "klokke" is also in "en kirkeklokke" (a church bell). To say someone rings it, use "at ringe på" (to ring): "Hun ringer på dørklokken" (She rings the doorbell).

sentence.da: Der er en **dørklokke** ved vores hoveddør.
sentence.en: There is a doorbell by our front door.

en dørmåtte.explanation: "En dørmåtte" means "a doormat". It is built from "en dør" (a door) and "en måtte" (a mat). The part "måtte" is also in "en yogamåtte" (a yoga mat).

sentence.da: Der ligger en **dørmåtte** foran vores dør.
sentence.en: There is a doormat in front of our door.

et daggry.explanation: "Et daggry" means "a dawn". To talk about the moment the sun comes up, use "en solopgang" (a sunrise) instead: "Vi så solopgangen på stranden" (We watched the sunrise on the beach).

sentence.da: Fuglene begynder at synge ved **daggry**, før solen står op.
sentence.en: The birds start to sing at dawn, before the sun rises.

et dankort.explanation: "Et dankort" means "a Dankort", the Danish debit card. To ask if you can pay with it, say: "Kan jeg betale med dankort?" (Can I pay by Dankort?). After "med" (with), Danish leaves out "et".

sentence.da: I Danmark bruger mange **dankort** i butikken.
sentence.en: In Denmark many people use Dankort in stores.

et danskkursus.explanation: "Et danskkursus" means "a Danish course". It is built from "dansk" (Danish) and "et kursus" (a course). The part "kursus" is also in "et førstehjælpskursus" (a first aid course).

sentence.da: Hun har **danskkursus** om aftenen.
sentence.en: She has Danish class in the evening.

et decimaltal.explanation: "Et decimaltal" means "a decimal number". It is built from "decimal" and "et tal" (a number). Danish writes a comma where English writes a point, so "2,5" is read "to komma fem" (two point five).

sentence.da: Tallet 3,5 er et **decimaltal**.
sentence.en: The number 3.5 is a decimal number.

et demokrati.explanation: "Et demokrati" means "a democracy". To describe a country with this system, use the adjective "demokratisk" (democratic): "Det er et demokratisk land" (It is a democratic country).

sentence.da: I et **demokrati** må man frit sige sin mening.
sentence.en: In a democracy, people may freely say their opinion.

et depositum.explanation: "Et depositum" means "a deposit", as in the money a landlord holds when you rent a home. To say you get it back, use "at få tilbage" (to get back): "Jeg får mit depositum tilbage" (I get my deposit back).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler et **depositum**, når jeg flytter ind.
sentence.en: I pay a deposit when I move in.

et diagram.explanation: "Et diagram" means "a chart". It also means "a diagram" in English: "Diagrammet viser, hvordan en motor virker" (The diagram shows how an engine works).

sentence.da: Læreren viser et **diagram** med søjler og tal.
sentence.en: The teacher shows a chart with columns and numbers.

et digt.explanation: "Et digt" means "a poem". It comes from the verb "at digte" (to write poetry). To say you write one, use "at skrive" (to write): "Hun skriver et digt til sin mor" (She writes a poem for her mother).

sentence.da: Hun læser et smukt **digt** højt for klassen.
sentence.en: She reads a beautiful poem aloud to the class.

et diktatur.explanation: "Et diktatur" means "a dictatorship". To say where people live, use "at leve i" (to live in): "Mange mennesker lever i et diktatur" (Many people live in a dictatorship).

sentence.da: I et **diktatur** er der ingen frie valg.
sentence.en: In a dictatorship, there are no free elections.

et diplom.explanation: "Et diplom" means "a diploma". To talk about a small certificate for taking part in something, use "et diplom for deltagelse" (a certificate for taking part): "Alle børn fik et diplom for deltagelse" (All the children got a certificate for taking part).

sentence.da: Efter eksamen får man et **diplom** som bevis på uddannelsen.
sentence.en: After the exam, you get a diploma as proof of your studies.

et distrikt.explanation: "Et distrikt" means "a district". To talk about the area a school covers, use "et skoledistrikt" (a school district): "Vi bor i samme skoledistrikt" (We live in the same school district).

sentence.da: Politiet har ansvaret for sikkerheden i hvert **distrikt**.
sentence.en: The police are responsible for safety in each district.

et dobbeltværelse.explanation: "Et dobbeltværelse" means "a double room". It is built from "dobbelt" (double) and "et værelse" (a room). To book one, say how long you stay with "til" (for): "Jeg vil gerne booke et dobbeltværelse til to nætter" (I would like to book a double room for two nights).

sentence.da: Vi to vil gerne have et **dobbeltværelse**.
sentence.en: The two of us would like a double room.

et dokument.explanation: "Et dokument" means "a document". To tell someone to save one on the computer, use "at gemme" (to save): "Husk at gemme dokumentet" (Remember to save the document).

sentence.da: Jeg skal skrive under på et **dokument**.
sentence.en: I have to sign a document.

et download.explanation: "Et download" means "a download". It comes from the English word. The action is "at downloade" (to download): "Jeg downloader filen" (I am downloading the file).

sentence.da: Dit **download** er færdigt, og filen ligger på skrivebordet.
sentence.en: Your download is finished, and the file is on the desktop.

et drab.explanation: "Et drab" means "a killing". To say what a news story is about, use "om" (about) after the verb: "Avisen skriver om et drab i Aarhus" (The paper writes about a killing in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Politiet efterforsker et **drab**, som skete i nat.
sentence.en: The police are investigating a homicide that happened last night.

et drama.explanation: "Et drama" means "a drama". To say someone makes a big fuss over little, use it for the fuss: "Hvorfor al det drama?" (Why all the drama?).

sentence.da: Filmen er et **drama** om to søstre, der skændes.
sentence.en: The movie is a drama about two sisters who argue.

et drivhus.explanation: "Et drivhus" means "a greenhouse". To say what you grow there, use "at dyrke" (to grow): "Vi dyrker agurker i drivhus" (We grow cucumbers in a greenhouse). The part "drivhus" is also in "drivhuseffekten" (the greenhouse effect) and "drivhusgasser" (greenhouse gases).

sentence.da: Tomaterne vokser hurtigt i et varmt **drivhus**.
sentence.en: The tomatoes grow fast in a warm greenhouse.

et drømmejob.explanation: "Et drømmejob" means "a dream job". It is built from "en drøm" (a dream) and "et job" (a job). Here "drøm" means a wish, not a dream you have while you sleep: "Hendes drøm er at blive kok" (Her dream is to become a cook).

sentence.da: Endelig har jeg fået mit **drømmejob** som kok.
sentence.en: I have finally gotten my dream job as a cook.

et dukketeater.explanation: "Et dukketeater" means "a puppet theater". It is built from "en dukke" (a puppet or doll) and "et teater" (a theater). The part "teater" is also in "et børneteater" (a children's theater).

sentence.da: Børnene sidder foran et **dukketeater** og ser dukkerne spille.
sentence.en: The children sit in front of a puppet theater and watch the puppets perform.

et dusin.explanation: "Et dusin" means "a dozen". To say a dozen of something, put the thing right after it, with no word for "of": "et dusin roser" (a dozen roses).

sentence.da: Et **dusin** æg er tolv æg.
sentence.en: A dozen eggs is twelve eggs.

et dynebetræk.explanation: "Et dynebetræk" means "a duvet cover". It is built from "en dyne" (a duvet) and "et betræk" (a cover). The part "betræk" is also used for furniture: "et sofabetræk" (a sofa cover).

sentence.da: Dynen ligger inde i et **dynebetræk**.
sentence.en: The duvet is inside a duvet cover.

et dyr.explanation: "Et dyr" means "an animal". To talk about an animal that lives free in nature, say "et vildt dyr" (a wild animal): "Vi så et vildt dyr i skoven" (We saw a wild animal in the forest).

sentence.da: Hunde og katte er **dyr**.
sentence.en: Dogs and cats are animals.

et dyreinternat.explanation: "Et dyreinternat" means "an animal shelter". To say you take in a pet from there, use "at adoptere" (to adopt): "Vi adopterer en hund fra et dyreinternat" (We are adopting a dog from an animal shelter).

sentence.da: Hunde og katte uden hjem bor i et **dyreinternat**.
sentence.en: Dogs and cats without a home live in an animal shelter.

et dæk.explanation: "Et dæk" means "a tire or deck". When you talk about the rubber part of a wheel, use it for the tire: "Jeg skal have nye dæk til bilen" (I need new tires for the car). When you talk about a floor of a ship, use it for the deck: "Skibet har tre dæk" (The ship has three decks).

sentence.da: Bilen har et fladt **dæk**.
sentence.en: The car has a flat tire.

et døgn.explanation: "Et døgn" means "a day (24 hours)". To say something is open all day and night, use "hele døgnet" (all day and night): "Butikken er åben hele døgnet" (The store is open all day and night). Do not mix it up with "en dag" (a day), which can also mean only the daytime: "Det er lyst om dagen" (It is light during the day).

sentence.da: Der er fireogtyve timer i et **døgn**.
sentence.en: There are twenty-four hours in a day.

et dørslag.explanation: "Et dørslag" means "a colander". To say you rinse vegetables in it, use "at skylle" (to rinse): "Jeg skyller grøntsagerne i dørslaget" (I rinse the vegetables in the colander).

sentence.da: Jeg hælder pastaen i et **dørslag**.
sentence.en: I pour the pasta into a colander.
